caption: Get Info rows on an exact LABEL_ROW + TIGHT grid, window sized to its content.

caption: Sortable ColumnListView with 16 px icons; count and free space in the bar beside the scroll bar.

caption: BeOS-style inline rename replaces the Rename dialog: the field sits on the label's own baseline and lines up with the selection highlight; the name without its extension starts selected.

title: Tracker: column view
caption: macOS-style column view (⌘4): one column per folder level, auto-hiding scroll bars, and a preview pane with an async thumbnail and file facts.

caption: Find takes focus on open, closes with ⌘W, shows home-relative locations and a baseline-aligned status.

title: Menus: shortcut glyphs on the baseline
caption: ⌘, ⇧ and arrows come from a fallback font; each is now laid out separately so it shares the item's baseline. The Trash is titled Trash.

title: Tracker: Find searches contents with ripgrep
caption: Find is built on ripgrep's crates (ignore + grep-searcher): parallel walk, smart case, .gitignore-aware, binary files skipped. Contents matches show the line number and text; live progress, Stop/Escape cancel.

title: Tracker Status: background file operations
caption: Copy, move, duplicate, Trash and Empty Trash run on worker threads (copy_file_range in chunks). Jobs longer than 0.4 s appear here with bytes, items, current file and time left; Stop cancels and removes the partial copy.

title: In-place reload: before

title: In-place reload: after an upgrade
caption: After tabula-session reload with new tabula-session, app_server and Tracker binaries: the session re-executed itself, restarted app_server, and Tracker re-executed with its saved state. Pixel-identical to the screenshot before.

title: Tracker: live updates
caption: Folder windows, columns and the desktop now follow the disk as it changes via inotify, with no polling. Shot 120 ms after a shell wrote download.iso, renamed notes.md, deleted photo-02.jpg and made Archive. Selection and sort are kept; a deleted folder says so.

title: Terminal (light)
caption: Tabula Light scheme: 16 ANSI colours tuned for contrast on paper white, SGR attributes and truecolor, CJK/Greek/symbol fallback fonts, box drawing drawn as geometry (rounded and heavy), block elements, a kitty-protocol inline image, and a compiler-style path link.

title: Terminal (dark)
caption: The same session in Tabula Dark (graphite, soft pastels). The scheme follows the desktop theme, and OSC 10/11 colour queries answer from it, so TUIs like Claude Code choose the matching theme.

title: Quick Look: images
caption: Space on a selected item opens Quick Look; the window fits the screen (app_server now keeps newly sized windows on screen) and follows the selection.

title: Quick Look: source code (dark)
caption: Text and code coloured by syntax with the shared kit syntax palette (the same hues as Terminal), line numbers, virtualised rows.

title: Quick Look: every format (dark)
caption: Contact sheet: MP3/OGG with tags and playback, Markdown, JPEG, tar.gz, SVG, PDF (hayro), CSV, PNG, Word, zip, Rust. All decoded in process, with no helper tools.

title: Viewer: PDF form filling (light)
caption: Text, comb, combo, list box, radio and check fields filled in place, with a placed signature.

caption: Unsaved text and styles came back after app_server reloaded and the app re-executed; default text follows the theme, explicit colours stay.

caption: The warning, stop, info and idea alert icons were missing from the set (every alert drew none); generated against the reference set.

caption: Headless 2x session: StyledEdit asks for the text cursor over cursor-shape-v1, the desktop shows the hand, the window frame shows the resize arrow.

caption: app_server panel for the brightness and volume keys and Ctrl+Cmd+A caffeinated, light and dark, 2x.

caption: Right-click the cup (also in the Tabula menu): until turned off, 1 to 8 hours, even with the lid closed, Allow Sleep with the end time. The menu now flips to stay on screen.

caption: Keyboard illumination keys raise the backlight with the level indicator; Preferences Keyboard has a Backlight slider that follows it. Turns off with the display.

caption: Find in the scrollback: case, whole words, wrap-around, backwards

caption: The match is selected and scrolled into view; Find Again steps on

title: Colour emoji in Terminal
caption: COLRv1 emoji painted natively: sequences, skin tones, flags, keycaps, on any background

title: Icons for document kinds
caption: Spreadsheet, presentation, word processing, PDF and font files get their own icons

title: Viewer zoom and pan
caption: Images load at full resolution in Viewer: Actual Size, pinch and command-scroll zoom about the pointer, drag to pan

title: Viewer: AVIF
caption: AVIF decoded natively with avif-parse and the BSD-licensed rav1d AV1 decoder, with our own YUV to RGB; HEIC through heifer and Ogg Opus playback through opus-decoder land in the same change

title: Viewer: video playback
caption: H.264 in mp4 and Matroska decoded with OpenH264 a few frames ahead and shown against a clock that follows the sound; play, pause, seek and replay, and the screen stays awake while it plays

title: Viewer: AV1 video
caption: AV1 in WebM and Matroska plays through rav1d with Opus sound; the poster frame decodes too, and the YUV to RGB conversion moved to fixed point tables (1080p at 72 frames a second)

title: Network: joining enterprise Wi-Fi
caption: A sheet for 802.1X networks: PEAP or TTLS with username and password, or TLS with certificate and key, the CA and a domain; shown with made-up networks. Tab now moves between text fields in every kit form

title: NetPositive in dark mode
caption: The new Servo based browser: tabs, toolbar and location field follow the theme while pages stay light

title: NetPositive error page
caption: Network errors answer in haiku, as NetPositive did, picked at random from six new verses

title: Passwords: Password Generator
caption: Random, memorable and PIN recipes with a live strength meter; Use fills the field it was opened from.

title: Passwords: a 1Password browser
caption: Tabula's password manager, on its own Rust 1Password SDK over the desktop app's integration socket (shown against the test fake): vaults and categories, items, and the selected item's fields.

title: Passwords: locked
caption: Opens locked and locks after idle; Touch ID (fprintd) or the account password (PAM) unlocks it.

title: NetPositive: logins from Passwords
caption: The key button lists the page's logins from Passwords (starting and unlocking it if need be) and fills the chosen one in.

title: NetPositive: offer to update a login
caption: After a sign-in with a changed password, NetPositive offers to update the login in Passwords; a new one gets Save.

title: NetPositive: save a passkey
caption: A page's navigator.credentials.create() asks in a bar; Passwords makes and keeps the key.

title: NetPositive: sign in with a passkey
caption: navigator.credentials.get() finds the site's passkeys in Passwords and asks before Passwords signs.

title: NetPositive: choosing a passkey
caption: With several passkeys for the site, the bar has a pop-up to choose the account.

title: Passwords: a passkey in a login
caption: Passkeys live in a Passkey section of a 1Password login: credential ID, relying party, user, and the concealed P-256 key.

title: NetPositive: Find
caption: Edit ▸ Find… (⌘F) and Find Again (⌘G): a BeOS Find window; the match is selected and scrolled to the middle.

title: NetPositive: Downloads
caption: Downloads go straight to ~/Downloads on a worker thread: links the page can't show, download links (also blob: and data: ones made by script), and Download Linked File / Download Image in the context menu. The Downloads window shows live progress and rate, with Stop, Retry, Open and Show.

title: NetPositive: scroll bars
caption: Servo draws no scroll bars, so a script reports where the page is scrolled and NetPositive draws BeOS ones beside it (a new kit ScrollBar): the vertical bar always, the horizontal one when the page is wider than the window. Dragging, paging and the arrows scroll the page.

title: NetPositive: tab icons
caption: Tabs show the page's favicon (scaled on the CPU to a crisp 16-point icon), or a plain document for pages without one.

title: Preferences: Backgrounds' BColorControl
caption: The desktop colour is now set with the kit's new ColorControl, BeOS's BColorControl: grey, red, green and blue ramps from black with draggable markers, and number fields.

title: NetPositive: colour picker
caption: <input type=color> opens a Choose a Colour sheet with the kit ColorControl; OK sets the page's colour and fires its input and change events (Servo 0.7 fires none).

title: NetPositive: dark pages
caption: In dark and night modes pages that support dark (color-scheme, prefers-color-scheme) go dark, canvas included; pages that don't stay black on white with light form controls and links.

title: NetPositive: light page, dark desktop
caption: A page with no colour scheme in dark mode: Servo would have drawn it with light text and dark controls on white; it now keeps the light scheme.

title: NetPositive: audio and video
caption: Video and audio elements in pages play with Tabula's own decoders (H.264/AV1 in MP4 and WebM, Opus, AAC, MP3 and more) through a native servo-media backend; sound goes to the sound server in process.

title: NetPositive: a page over its memory
caption: A page that runs away with memory meets its unit's MemoryMax (512 MiB here, for the test) and is OOM-killed alone; the bar says why, over the crash page.

title: NetPositive: a stuck page
caption: Pages run in content processes, each a systemd unit with its own memory limit and CPU weight. A tab whose page stops answering for ten seconds gets this bar; Stop Page kills just that process and the tab shows the crash page.

title: NetPositive: a page of 120 big photos
caption: 120 pictures of 2400×1600, 1.8 GB once decoded. The page's process now holds only their files (60 MB, was every bitmap), and the painter decodes a picture only while it's drawn, within 128 MB shared by every page, so the whole browser stays near 600 MB however long the page.

title: NetPositive: a call, end to end
caption: Two RTCPeerConnections in one page, talking through NetPositive's own WebRTC (webrtc-rs, in process). The fake camera's test card goes out as H.264 (openh264) and comes back decoded on the right; the microphone goes as Opus and plays; a data channel carries text and bytes both ways; getStats() counts the pictures.

title: Deskbar: a new build is ready
caption: tabula-session watches the tree Tabula was built in. Once a build finishes with newer programs, a green arrow appears in Deskbar's tray; clicking it asks before installing them and reloading the session in place (windows stay open).

title: NetPositive: the WebRTC samples' peer connection
caption: The official webrtc.github.io 'Peer connection' sample, unmodified: the test camera (left) goes through two RTCPeerConnections and comes back decoded (right), connected in 281 ms.

title: Passwords: choose your 1Password account
caption: Setting up Passwords now lists the accounts signed in to the 1Password app (read from its local account summaries), with email and sign-in address, instead of asking for a name or UUID. Another account still takes one by hand.

title: Keyring prompts are Tabula's
caption: gnome-keyring asks for the login keyring's password through a system prompter; the authentication agent now is that prompter (gcr's protocol and encrypted secret exchange, in Rust), so unlocking it for gh or a browser is a Tabula alert, not GTK's gcr-prompter. A wrong password comes back with the keyring's warning.

title: Shells that outlive Terminal
caption: Terminal's shells now run in tabula-termd, one per display, which keeps each screen too. Quit Terminal, or have it crash or upgrade, and the next one reopens a window on every shell as it was, scrollback, vim and all. Terminal ▸ Terminal Daemon… shows it and its shells, and can restart it in place (shells kept) or start it over.

title: Images survive Terminal crashes
caption: Terminal was killed after showing a kitty image; tabula-termd relaunched it and replayed the screen, image included. ⌘R also reaches the shell now (reverse history search).

title: Zoom leaves Deskbar alone
caption: A zoomed window now stops 4 px short of Deskbar, as on BeOS, instead of running under it.

title: Right-click in text fields
caption: Every text field now has Cut, Copy, Paste and Select All on right-click (keeping the selection), and double/triple-click select a word or the whole line, here in NetPositive's location field.

title: Brightness for every display
caption: Preferences ▸ Display now has a brightness slider for each display whose brightness can be set, external monitors too (the Studio Display over USB). Every display starts at full brightness unless you've set a level for it.

title: Tile windows from the keyboard
caption: ⇧⌘← and ⇧⌘→ tile the window into half the display, ⇧⌘↑/↓ the top or bottom; ⌃⌘↵ tiles every window on the display (here, three); quarters, thirds, centering and moving to the next display too. Space between them and at the edges is set in Preferences.

title: Keyboard shortcuts in Preferences
caption: Keyboard ▸ Shortcuts lists the desktop's shortcuts, with the space around tiled windows. Click one and type new keys (here Left half became ⌃⌥L); keys taken from another shortcut are said, and Default Keys puts them all back.

title: Notifications
caption: A native notification centre: apps' notifications (org.freedesktop.Notifications) appear as cards in the lower right with the app's icon, the summary, the body and their actions. A click is the default action; they go by themselves unless critical, and wait while the pointer is over them.

title: NetPositive: web notifications
caption: Sites can show notifications: the first time one asks, a bar over its tab offers Allow or Don’t Allow (remembered per site); allowed notifications appear in the desktop's notification centre, and a click brings the tab forward.

title: NetPositive: dark pages
caption: View ▸ Dark Pages (Automatic, the default, follows the desktop; Always; Never). Each frame is redrawn on the GPU through a shader that turns lightness around and keeps hues, so every page goes dark, blank ones included; pictures, video and canvases are pre-inverted with the CSS filter the shader undoes, and pages that are dark already are left alone. Left: Never; right: Always.

title: Command palette (⌘Space)
caption: ⌘Space opens a Raycast-style palette over everything: apps, the front app's menu commands, files, Passwords items, Preferences, windows, a calculator and every desktop shortcut with its keys, so typing "half" doubles as a reminder of ⇧⌘←.

title: NetPositive: dark pages, the Chrome way
caption: Dark pages redone as Chrome's Auto Dark Mode for Web Contents: WebRender recolours what each thing is (light backgrounds and borders go dark, dark text light, by CIELAB lightness with hue kept), so photos, gradients and coloured buttons keep their true colours and only icons that Chrome's classifier would flip are inverted. Left: light desktop; right: dark.

title: Quick Look: F for fullscreen
caption: In Quick Look, F fills the screen with the preview and F again puts it back in its window at the size it had (Cx::set_fullscreen, new in the kit).

title: Tracker: column view scrolls sideways
caption: Columns wider than the window scroll sideways with the touchpad, Shift+wheel or a scroll bar along the bottom, and stay where they were put; the view only follows the keyboard when the selection moves to another column.

title: NetPositive learns login fields
caption: The field menu now lists the page's logins at once (fetched when the page loads). Filling an odd field from it — here 'who are you' as the username — is remembered for that page, so the key button fills the same field next time. Hidden decoy fields, as on Google's sign-in, are skipped.

title: Preferences ▸ Tracker
caption: New Tracker windows open in column view by default; Preferences has a Tracker panel to choose the view new windows open in, and Tracker follows a change at once.

title: Deskbar: a click lists an app's windows
caption: Clicking an application with more than one window in Deskbar now opens its window menu to pick one (or Show All); with one window it comes forward at once, as before.

title: Find: Space for Quick Look
caption: In Tracker's Find window, Space shows the selected result in Quick Look and the arrow keys step through the results, as in a folder window. A space typed into the Find field still goes into the query.

title: Tracker: Open in Terminal
caption: File ▸ Open in Terminal, and the context menus, open a new Terminal window in the folder shown, or in the right-clicked folder (here alpha).

title: Passwords: setup offers sync or local
caption: Passwords now keeps its own encrypted store. The first time, it asks whether to sync with a 1Password account (both ways) or keep items only on this computer.

title: Passwords: its own store, synced with 1Password
caption: Items are read from the local encrypted store at once; 1Password is only for syncing, in the background. The status line shows the last sync.

title: Passwords: changes wait while 1Password is away
caption: With 1Password not running, changes are kept and the status line counts what's still to send; they go up on the next sync.

title: Videos with B-frames play properly
caption: H.264 High videos with B-frames (most from screen recorders and x264) played with good sound but a picture that jumped and stalled: OpenH264 was asked to flush a picture after every packet, which broke reordering, so every B-frame failed. Now every picture decodes, in display order and in step with the sound (edit lists applied); seeking WebM/AV1 lands on the right frame too.

title: NetPositive asks before quitting
caption: Quitting NetPositive (or closing a window) with several tabs open, or downloads still running, now asks first, so a stray ⌘Q doesn't throw the tabs away.

title: Passwords asks before syncing anything
caption: Syncing with 1Password now works out every change first, both ways (adding, changing, archiving, deleting, with the parts that differ), and makes none until you approve them in Review Sync. Automatic syncs only say how many changes are waiting.

title: Restore from the Trash
caption: Items in the Trash can go back where they came from: Restore in the File menu or an item's menu puts them back in their folders (made again if gone), and never over something new in their place.

title: Passwords: every vault, and sync problems you can read
caption: 1Password won't let other apps read archived items, and one archived item failed a whole batch of fifty, so most of Personal and Private never arrived. Now only active items are fetched, an item archived there is archived here from its listing, and a failed batch is retried one item at a time. What still can't sync is listed in a Sync Problems window, grouped by vault, each with its reason, instead of a wall of red text.

title: Passwords: several 1Password accounts
caption: Passwords now syncs with every 1Password account you tick (File ▸ 1Password Accounts…), in one review. The sidebar lists each account's vaults under its name, a vault is named with its account wherever it could be confused, and removing an account asks first and only removes its items from this computer.

title: Drag and drop
caption: Files drag between Tracker's views, the desktop, other apps and other Wayland programs, BeOS-style: a see-through picture with the name, folders light up to take them, move within a disk and copy across, a right-button drag asks Move/Copy/Link. Desktop icons stay where you put them. Drop a file on Terminal to type its path (an image into Claude Code).

title: Band selection in lists
caption: Dragging from a row's other columns, or from below the rows, draws a selection band in Tracker's list view and in every kit list (⇧ or ⌘ adds; it scrolls on near the edges). The column view does the same from below a column's items.

title: Security preferences
caption: Preferences ▸ Security holds how Passwords keeps its secrets: sync with 1Password automatically or only when asked, lock after idle, lock when the screen locks, and how soon copied secrets leave the clipboard. Passwords follows them live.

title: Google Chrome, installed on first use
caption: Google Chrome is one of Tabula's applications. The first time it is opened, Tabula offers to download it from Google's own repository, checks it against the repository's checksum, unpacks it natively into the home folder and starts it, drawing with Wayland in a Tabula window.

title: GTK and Chrome in Tabula's colours
caption: The desktop portals now start in a real session. GTK 3, GTK 4 and libadwaita apps take Tabula's palette, fonts and close-left/zoom-right buttons, in light and dark, and Chrome opens with Tabula's tab and frame instead of its own buttons.

title: Log Viewer
caption: A native reader for your journal: Tabula's own programs (or everything), by level and time, with Find, live tail, Show in Context and syntax highlighting on every line. Also a --print command line for agents.

title: Hide window, anywhere
caption: ⌘M hides the window in front, Tabula's or any other app's, and Hide window is a ⌘Space command (it finds "minimize" too). Change the keys in Preferences ▸ Keyboard.

title: Long menus scroll
caption: A menu taller than the screen fits it now, with BeOS scroll arrows at its ends: rest the pointer on one to scroll, or use the wheel or the arrow keys.

title: Notifications, grouped
caption: Notifications now gather under their app as on Haiku, keep bold, italics and links, show progress, take a reply in place, and wear a blue edge when important or a red one for errors. A click hands the app an activation token so its window comes forward.

title: Notification history
caption: The History window (Deskbar's bell, or tabula-notifications --history): every notification newest first, kept across a restart. Click to act on it (or bring the app forward), × to forget one; Do Not Disturb and Clear All along the top.

title: Deskbar's notification bell
caption: The bell counts unread notifications; click for the history, right-click for Do Not Disturb (now, for an hour, until morning) and the settings. Struck through while quiet.

title: Preferences ▸ Notifications
caption: Do Not Disturb by hand or every day at set times, how long banners stay, and per-app banners, sounds and history (apps appear once they have notified). Dark theme.

title: GApplication notifications
caption: tabula-notifications now also serves GLib's org.gtk.Notifications: a GApplication's notification (here a test app's, with an app.reply button) shows like any other, and its actions run on the app over org.freedesktop.Application.

title: Tracker says when a long copy is done
caption: Through the kit's new notify API: a copy or move that ran 10 s or more posts “Finished copying …”; clicking it shows the folder.

title: Viewer: crop a picture
caption: Image ▸ Crop… puts a frame over the picture: drag one out, move it or pull its edges; the size shows below and the rest dims. Crop (or Return) keeps it, and the title says the picture is edited until it's saved.

title: Viewer: Adjust Size
caption: Image ▸ Adjust Size… resizes the picture, keeping its proportions unless asked not to. Rotate, flip, crop and resize can all be undone, and File ▸ Save writes the picture back in its own format (Save As for another).

title: Quick Look rotates pictures
caption: Quick Look's footer has Rotate Left and Right (⌘L and ⌘R), which turn the picture and save it at once, as on the Mac. Anything more opens in Viewer.

title: Preferences: Backup
caption: Export saves every Tabula setting and piece of saved state in one .tabula-backup file. Import shows what a backup holds, app by app, and asks before replacing anything; the settings as they were are saved first.

title: Backup, dark
caption: The Backup panel in the dark theme.

title: Backups have their own icon
caption: Tracker shows .tabula-backup files with the new backup icon; opening one shows it in Preferences ▸ Backup, ready to import.

title: Drag a picture out of Viewer
caption: A picture that fits Viewer's window drags out as its file (and, for PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP, the picture itself for programs that take one). Quick Look does the same, from the picture or its footer's icon. Dropping it back into its own folder is refused.

title: Drop files on an app in Deskbar
caption: Files dragged onto a running application in Deskbar highlight it and open with it when dropped.

title: Spring-loaded folders
caption: Rest a drag on a folder for a second and it opens, so the drag can go on into it (here a file dragged onto Dest, whose window opened under the pointer).

title: Views scroll under a drag
caption: A drag held near the top or bottom of any scrolling view scrolls it on, faster nearer the edge, so a drop can reach what was out of view.

title: GTK windows wear Tabula's chrome
caption: Plain GTK 3 and GTK 4 windows (no headerbar) now get Tabula's tab and frame: app_server speaks KDE's server-decoration protocol, which is how GTK asks for server-side decorations.

title: Drag an application out of Deskbar
caption: Dragging an application's row out of Deskbar leaves a link to it where it's dropped, named and drawn as the application; opening the link starts it.

title: Drag text in and out of text fields
caption: Press on selected text and drag it: within a StyledEdit document it moves (styles and all), into another field or app it's copied, onto a folder it becomes a clipping. A caret shows where it will land.

title: Drag a field out of Passwords
caption: Drag a username, password, one-time code or website from an item onto another app's field; the drag shows the field's name, never the secret.

title: DriveSetup
caption: A new app for disks, after BeOS's DriveSetup: a map of the chosen disk over every disk, partition and unlocked volume. Mount, unlock, format (optionally encrypted), create, resize, rename and delete partitions, new partition tables, write a disk image, eject, check health and benchmark, all through UDisks on worker threads with live progress and Stop. The disk holding the running system is never offered for anything destructive. Shown against udisks-fake, never real disks.

title: Passwords in Chrome
caption: A field's context menu in Chrome now has Passwords: each login for the page, with its username, password, one-time code or the whole login. A Tabula extension, installed and kept up to date by tabula-chrome itself, talks to Passwords through tabula-chrome as its native messaging host; the toolbar button lists the page's logins, and a login sent with a form is offered for saving or updating.

title: Agent Screens
caption: Agents get screens of their own: each is a whole Tabula desktop with its own windows, pointer and keyboard focus, so an agent never moves your pointer or takes your focus. tabula-screen starts one and drives it (run, look, windows, click, type, key); the Agent Screens window shows it live, and Take Control lets you step in.

title: Chrome's notifications in Tabula
caption: Google Chrome's notifications now come to Tabula's notifications app: a site's notification shows with Chrome's name and icon and the site as a link, a click goes back to the page, and Chrome's Settings button opens its notification settings.

title: Other programs survive an app_server restart
caption: GNOME Text Editor kept its window through tabula-wlproxy: the first line typed before app_server restarted, the second after, with no reconnect in the app.

title: Deskbar: the date and time on their own row, an Agent Screens item
caption: The tray's clock moves to a row of its own (date on the left, time on the right; click for Date & Time), so the well below holds only status icons, each 16 px on a 22 px grid, centred and wrapping to more rows when they don't fit. While agent screens run, a monitor with a pointer shows (with a count when there are several); clicking it opens Agent Screens.

title: Tiled windows move together when one is resized
caption: Activity Monitor tiled to the left half, StyledEdit top right, Preferences bottom right; dragging Preferences' left edge leftwards moved the whole split: Activity Monitor narrower, both right-hand windows wider, the gap kept. Only windows tiled by a tiling command take part; one moved or sized by hand on its own is never pushed. Neighbours stop at their apps' minimum sizes, and the parts they end up with are kept (also across a reload).

title: Notifications history: denser, with views
caption: Two-line rows (icon, bold title with app and time, a line of body), a dot for what is new, day headings and search; List, By App and Cards shown, Conversations stacks a thread. The selected note opens to its whole body and actions.

title: op asks Passwords
caption: Tabula's op answers scripts that use 1Password's op command (op inject, read, run, item get, whoami). The first time a terminal asks, Passwords names the command, who ran it and where, and Allow covers that terminal until Passwords locks.

title: Preferences: op on or off
caption: Preferences ▸ Security has a Command line box to turn op off; it's on by default.

title: Terminal tabs
caption: Terminal windows hold tabs: ⌘T opens one in the same folder, ⌘[ and ⌘] or Ctrl+Tab move between them, and tabs drag to reorder. A bell in a hidden tab marks it with a dot; Move Tab to New Window splits one off. The window grows by the strip so the grid stays the same, and tabs come back after an upgrade.

title: Terminal knows its coding agents
caption: Claude Code or Codex in a tab is recognized natively: the tab wears its state (a turning arc while it works, an orange ! when it asks, a green dot when its turn is done) and, when you're looking elsewhere, a notification says it needs you; Show brings that tab forward.

title: Notifications: Open and Dismiss
caption: A selected notification's default action now always reads Open (apps often call it Activate), and Dismiss sits beside it: on a conversation it dismisses every notification in it, on a single one just that one. Its buttons no longer overlap.

title: A window menu on the tab
caption: Right-clicking a window's yellow tab opens its menu: Hide, Zoom, Back to Its Own Size, Center, every tiling choice, Move to Workspace, Send to Back (what the right-click used to do) and Close, the same commands as the shortcuts and the palette.

title: New Window for a running app
caption: Right-clicking a running Tabula app in Tracker (or opening its menu in Deskbar) offers New Window: the running copy opens another window, as BeOS's Deskbar did, instead of a second copy starting. Terminal, StyledEdit and Tracker answer it.

title: Banners in the Deskbar's column
caption: Notification banners are now as wide as the Deskbar and flush with the screen's edge beneath it, where there is usually nothing else, and more compact: the app's icon in the group's title, the text taking the width, buttons sharing it. Preferences adds Never to Show banners for (errors still show).

title: Token Pool
caption: Claude Code and Codex share several subscriptions through a loopback gateway: each request goes to the account whose quota resets soonest, out-of-quota accounts wait for their reset, sign-ins are refreshed and kept sealed, and usage is counted without keeping any content. Fixture accounts.

title: Num Lock on at start
caption: Num Lock now starts on, and Preferences ▸ Keyboard can turn that off; the Num Lock key still toggles it, and changing other keyboard settings keeps its state.

title: Token Pool: a heatmap of requests
caption: The requests going through the pool now light up as cells under the header, like Pulse's LEDs, and each account keeps a strip of its latest 25: green completed, yellow rate limited, red failed, grey cancelled. Click any cell for its model, client, time and tokens. The grid is the kit's new CellGrid.

title: Terminal: Show All Tabs
caption: Show All Tabs (⌘⇧D) puts every tab of a window on screen at once, each a live pane with its title over it; click one to type into it, marked in the group's colour. The tab strip is taller now, with the group's band kept clear of the icons.

title: Fan Out
caption: ⌃⌘/ stacks a display's windows with their tabs side by side, narrowing them to stay clear of the Deskbar; ⌃⌘Z undoes it.

title: DriveSetup: free space
caption: A Free column shows how full each mounted volume is, and the status line says how much is left; it stays current while the window is open.

title: The wallpaper pack
caption: Backgrounds offers the new wallpapers with previews; each follows light and dark mode live and comes in a 16:9 or ultrawide version for each screen.

title: Smart Tiling
caption: Smart Tile (⌃⇧⌘↩) shows a model the screen and what each window holds, then tiles them; the note says how and offers Undo. (Here a fake model answered.)

title: Preferences ▸ AI
caption: AI features go through the Token Pool, or an Anthropic key; Smart Tiling picks its model and how hard it thinks.

title: Longest window title
caption: A tab shows at most this many characters of its title, then an ellipsis (here 20; 100 by default).

title: Appearance: Longest window title
caption: The new slider in Preferences ▸ Appearance.

title: Roll up
caption: Double-click a tab (or ⌃⌘M, or Roll Up in its menu) and only the tab stays; again brings the window back.

title: Icons in the Deskbar menu
caption: Every item in Deskbar's Tabula menu now has its icon: the commands, our applications, the preference panels and each category of other applications. New sunburst icons for Stay Awake, Lock Screen, Log Out, Restart, Shut Down and the categories. Appearance ▸ Show icons in the Deskbar menu turns them off; it's on by default.

title: Deskbar menu icons in dark mode
caption: The Applications submenu in dark mode. The kit's popup menus take an icon on any item (Menu::icon), with a column that sits after the check marks when a menu has both.

title: Tabula is now Olo Desktop
caption: The new brand in About and Deskbar, light and dark: the mark and the olo wordmark, drawn crisp at 2× from data/brand. A running Tabula session upgrades into Olo in place, every window and setting kept.

title: OpenAI's models for AI features
caption: Preferences ▸ AI offers Astra 6 (the default), Sol 6.1, Terra 6.1 and Luna 6, reached through the Token Pool's Codex accounts. A Claude model chosen before reads as Astra; calls turned away for now are retried after a wait.

title: Keyboard hints
caption: Tapping Control and Shift together (opt-in, Preferences ▸ Keyboard ▸ Keyboard Hints) puts a letter on everything that can be picked: the focused window's controls, other windows by their tabs, Deskbar and the desktop's icons. Typing one picks it.

title: Keyboard hints in menus (dark)
caption: A pick that opens a menu letters its items next, skipping disabled ones; a submenu's come first.

title: Rolled-up windows share one tile
caption: Tile All with four of seven windows rolled up: the three open ones get a cell each, and the four rolled-up ones share the last cell, their tabs side by side along its top. Unrolling one fills that cell.

title: Rolled-up windows share one tile (dark)
caption: The same arrangement in dark mode.

title: Cascade Others
caption: ⌃⇧⌘\ with notes.txt focused: every other window is cascaded from the top left, and notes.txt stays where it was, in front. Fan Out Others (⌃⇧⌘/) does the same with Fan Out.

title: Deskbar: Window Arrangement
caption: The Olo menu now has the desktop-wide commands: Window Arrangement (Tile All, Smart Tile, Zoom All, Cascade All, Fan Out, Cascade and Fan Out Others, Undo), Workspaces and Show or Hide All Windows. The Deskbar tile shows the olo wordmark alone, centred.

title: Deskbar: Workspaces
caption: Go to a workspace, or move the window that had the focus to one.

title: Fan Out Others from the menu
caption: Chosen from Deskbar with README.md focused: the other windows fan out along the top and README.md stays where it was, in front.

title: Window groups
caption: An app's windows share one frame, with a tab each side by side along the top; clicking a tab brings that window forward. Group Windows in Deskbar's team menu or Tracker turns it off per app.

title: Window groups, dark
caption: The same group's tab bar in dark mode.

title: Palette: open windows first
caption: Typing an app's name in ⌘Space lists its open windows before the app itself, the one already in front last.

title: Twitcher: a row per workspace
caption: ⌘Tab shows a row of apps for each workspace with windows; ↑/↓ change rows and workspaces, ←/→ walk a row, Esc puts everything back. With keyboard hints on, each cell has a letter to pick it by.

title: Twitcher rows, dark
caption: The same, in dark mode.

title: Touchpad preferences: profiles and every tunable
caption: Preferences ▸ Touchpad now names the pad app_server found and recommends a profile (MacBook, Magic Trackpad, Standard; hand tuning makes it Custom). Touch holds Olo's palm and hover filter, a libinput plugin that counts a touch only while it presses, ignores palms and makes the click from the fingers' pressure alone; Gestures has scrolling speed, momentum glide, three-finger drag, drag lock and acceleration.

title: Touchpad preferences in dark
caption: The Touch, Gestures and Mouse tabs in dark mode.

title: DiskUsage: where the space went
caption: A new app: Haiku's DiskUsage ring chart (the folder in the middle, its contents in rings outwards; click to go in, the middle to go up) beside the folder's contents by size, with bars in the slices' colours, and DaisyDisk's Collector along the bottom: drag rows or slices in (or ⌘D), then Move to Trash or Delete. The scan runs on a worker and the chart grows as it goes; it stays on one file system and counts hard links once.

title: The DiskUsage icon
caption: A ring chart with a magnifier, generated against the reference set, beside DriveSetup and its neighbours on the light, dark and night panels.

title: Keyboard hints on a double Control
caption: Keyboard hints now come up when Control is pressed twice quickly, in place of Control and Shift together. How quickly is Preferences ▸ Keyboard ▸ Double-press speed (400 ms by default).

title: A link opened from outside comes forward
caption: A link opened from a shell or an agent (through olo-chrome) now takes you to the Chrome window it opened in, from whatever workspace: olo-chrome asks app_server for an activation token and Chrome uses it. Here the page was opened from workspace 3, and Olo moved to workspace 1, where the window is.

title: Preferences: Themes (dark)
caption: A new Themes panel picks the look of every icon and the Olo wordmark, in every app, the Deskbar and the desktop: Soft Be (the new default), BeBox, Toybox, Papercraft, Enamel, Halftone and Classic (Olo's first set). It applies at once, everywhere.

title: Preferences: Themes
caption: The Themes panel in light mode: each theme is shown by its wordmark and a row of its icons; Soft Be is the default.

title: Themes: the Deskbar and desktop in each theme
caption: The same Deskbar menu, Applications submenu and desktop icons in each of the seven themes, left to right and top to bottom: Soft Be, BeBox, Toybox, Papercraft, Enamel, Halftone and Classic. The wordmark and every app's icon change together.

title: Touchpad: the Touch tab ran into the buttons
caption: Before (left), the Touch tab ran past the bottom of the Touchpad window, so its last setting sat on top of the Defaults and Revert buttons. A first fix (right, 564 tall) clears the buttons but still squeezes the While Typing box at the bottom; the layout lint later measured it 12 px short, and the window is now 576 tall.

title: Zoom Vertically and Zoom Horizontally
caption: A window's menu can now zoom it along one axis only: Zoom Vertically makes it as tall as the screen and keeps its width and place across; Zoom Horizontally does the same the other way. Here the Themes window has been zoomed vertically. Alt+Shift+Cmd+Up or Down and Alt+Shift+Cmd+Left or Right do the same, as does double-clicking the window's top or bottom (or left or right) edge.

title: Keyboard: Option+Tab switches tabs
caption: Option+Tab and Option+Shift+Tab now move to the next and previous tab in any window that has tabs: Chrome, Terminal, Firefox, GTK and Qt apps and Olo's own tabbed windows. Like every shortcut, they can be changed in Keyboard. The new Zoom vertically and Zoom horizontally shortcuts are listed here too.

title: Power: before the layout lint
caption: Caught by the new layout lint (olo_kit::layout_lint): at 2× the Caffeinated box ran 1 px past the window's body, leaving 11 px above Defaults/Revert instead of WINDOW_INSET (12), and “Put the computer to sleep after:” stood 3 px from its field.

title: Power: after the layout lint
caption: One pixel taller (460×363) so the boxes clear the buttons by WINDOW_INSET, and the menu fields' divider moved out to 176 so the longest label has a LABEL_GAP before its field.

title: Tracker: before the layout lint
caption: The layout lint found the New Windows Open In box 1 px past the panel's body at 2× (11 px to the buttons, not 12).

title: Tracker: after the layout lint
caption: One pixel taller (300×181): the box ends WINDOW_INSET above Defaults/Revert.

title: About: wide enough for long facts
caption: The layout lint runs About with long real-world facts (e.g. “AMD Ryzen 9 7945HX with Radeon Graphics, 32 cores”); at 420 the processor was cut short with “…”, so About is now 440 wide.

title: Touchpad: 576 tall, measured by the layout lint
caption: The layout lint runs Touchpad with every pad and profile. Its worst case is a MacBook pad without pressure on Touch, which shows both notes. At 520 the While Typing box ran 56 px past the tab and over Defaults/Revert. At 564 it was still 12 px past at 2×, leaving 8 px instead of the box's 20 px inset. At 576 it fits. Without a pad (here) the notes aren't shown, so that room is left over.

title: A wallpaper for every theme
caption: Each theme now has its own wallpaper in the pack, light and dark, drawn in its material with the wordmark's o as the hero: BeBox, Soft Be, Toybox, Papercraft, Enamel, Halftone and Classic (rows, light then dark). BeBox's is the new default.

title: Themes switch the wallpaper too
caption: Choosing a theme in Preferences ▸ Themes now also sets the wallpaper to that theme's own (here Toybox); Backgrounds can still pick another.

title: Desktop menu over windows
caption: The desktop's right-click menu opened over a window was drawn behind it, and clicks went to the window. app_server now draws the desktop layer's menus over the windows and the Deskbar (under only the Overlay layer) and finds them there for the pointer and keyboard.

title: Terminal before the polish
caption: Show All Tabs before: square tabs cut off mid-letter, pane titles in plain panel grey, the screen's text right against the frame.

title: Terminal polished (dark)
caption: Rounded strip tabs that share the row and end long titles with '…', the group's name in a chip with a band of its colour on every tab, pane heads with icons, the pane being typed into marked in the group colour and the others dimmed, 8×6 padding around the screen. label_fit (elide with …) now used wherever a line can overflow: palette rows, Drive Setup, kit list messages.

title: Terminal polished (light)
caption: The same strip and padding in the light theme: the selected tab opens into the screen's own background (TabStrip::opens_into).

title: Quick Look: a window of its own, over Tracker
caption: Space in Tracker opens Quick Look as a dialog window (xdg_dialog_v1, parented to the Tracker window) instead of a tab: it is sized for the file, so it can be bigger than the folder window, opens centred over it before its first frame, and stays in front of it when the folder window is clicked.

title: Context menus show their keys
caption: Every context menu takes the keys its commands have in the window's menu bar (Menu::keys_from), so Tracker's item menu shows ⌘O, ⌘Y, ⌘I and so on, and the window tab menu shows the person's own desktop shortcuts.

title: Olo menu shows its shortcuts
caption: Deskbar's Olo menu shows the keys the person has for each desktop-wide command (Find, Window Arrangement, Show or Hide All Windows, Lock Screen), following changes in Keyboard preferences.

title: Minimized windows in Deskbar's window list
caption: An app's window list in Deskbar marks a minimized window as a Mac's Window menu does: a hollow diamond where the check mark goes and a lighter label. It can still be chosen to bring the window back; agents read minimized on the item.

title: Preferences ▸ Windows: space around arranged windows
caption: A new Windows panel sets the margin at the display's edges and the gap between windows, with a miniature of the main display that follows the sliders. Tiling, zooming, Tile All, Smart Tile, Center, cascading and fanning out all keep to it, and app_server refits tiled and zoomed windows live as the sliders move, without changing which window is in front. Here a margin of 26 and a gap of 12; Deskbar's Window Arrangement menu now ends with Windows Preferences….

title: Preferences ▸ Windows in dark mode
caption: The Windows panel in BeBox dark: the miniature's windows take the document colour and the theme's tab colours.

title: Terminal: Catppuccin colours
caption: Settings ▸ Colors offers Catppuccin Latte and Frappé for light mode, Macchiato and Mocha for dark; Frappé (left, light mode) and Macchiato (right, dark mode) are the defaults.

title: Deskbar on every display
caption: Preferences ▸ Display ▸ Show Deskbar on every display: each display gets its own Deskbar listing just the applications with windows there (main display left, second right, its only window just moved over).

title: Display preferences: Deskbar on every display
caption: The new check box under the display map, light and dark; the map draws a Deskbar on every display while it is on.

title: Window groups: ⌘-dragging a tab into another group
caption: Any window can be grouped by hand: ⌘-drag its tab over another window's (here Tracker's over Terminal's); it folds into its tab where it would go and that group lights up in the focus blue (light, dark). Let go, and it joins. ⌘-dragging a tab away pops the window out; along the tabs, it reorders them.

title: A new window joins its group at the group's size
caption: A Terminal opened from its own menu (Terminal ▸ New Terminal) joined its group, then the whole group shrank to the new window's default size: the menu's pointer grab lasts until the pointer next moves, sizes waited for any grab, and the new window, in front, then led the group at its own size. Now sizes wait only for a resize grab, and a window that joins a group by itself doesn't lead it until it has drawn at the group's size (asked again if its app draws another size anyway).

title: ⌘Space opens the palette on the display in use
caption: With two displays, the palette now opens on the focused window's display (here the Terminal on the right-hand one), else the pointer's, rather than always on the main display.

title: ⌘Tab groups windows by display
caption: With a Deskbar on every display, Twitcher's rows split into a column per display, each in an etched BBox named across its top with a little screen, lit on the display this copy of the panel is on, so it's clear which windows are where. ↑/↓ keep to the chosen window's display.

title: Terminal: tabs down the side
caption: Settings ▸ Tabs ▸ Down the Side stands the kit's TabStrip as a column (TabStrip::side): rows like Tracker's, the group's chip at the top and its band down each tab, the selected tab opening into the screen, and an edge to drag wider. The window keeps its size; the grid makes room.

title: Notifications: banners specialised per app
caption: Apps can say how a note looks (x-olo-* hints, olo_kit::notify's builders): an accent band, a badge and subtitle, a table of fields, a large picture, message or media styles. Websites through Chrome become their own apps (WhatsApp, Gmail) with their colours and monogram tiles; a message shows its sender round and the text in a balloon.

title: Notifications: unread first, fading with age
caption: The History window puts unread notes first under an Unread heading (lit dot, bold title, Mark All Read); clicking one reads it, and it keeps its place until the window closes. With fading on (Preferences, 1 hour by default) each row fades as it ages, the newest strongest, and goes once it has faded away; it shows at full strength while selected or under the pointer.

title: Terminal tabs without the lines
caption: The group shows as its chip alone: no coloured band under the strip, no separators beside the chip. The current tab is a raised page joined to the terminal below.

title: Terminal tabs down the side, Show All Tabs, dark
caption: Side tabs with the group's chip at the top and no band. In Show All Tabs the active pane's head is lit instead of edged.

title: Notification banners without the lines
caption: No accent band, top line or coloured edge. The app's colour is in its badge, tile and progress bar only; an error's title starts with a small crisp stop sign, level with the capitals, and there is more room around the icon.

title: Notification banners without the lines, dark
Notification cards without the lines, dark
caption: Cards are separated by space and an etched edge, not coloured bands; errors carry the stop sign.

title: Notification list: a stop sign for errors
caption: Rows lose their coloured kind edge; a failed note's title starts with the stop sign instead.

title: Preferences: fade notifications away over an hour
caption: History box: on by default, over 1 hour; the strip shows the fade from now to gone.

title: Preferences: notification fade, dark
caption: The same box in the dark theme.

title: Terminal: sudo asks for its password in a window
caption: When anything in a Terminal tab runs sudo (you at the prompt, or an agent like Claude Code with no terminal at all), Terminal asks in an alert of its own: who wants it, the command as typed, the fingerprint reader first if PAM uses it, then the password.

title: Terminal: the sudo window in dark mode
caption: While the fingerprint reader waits, the password field waits too; the note under it is what PAM says.

title: Terminal: sudo cancelled, plainly
caption: Cancel ends sudo with exit 1 and a line an agent can read: “sudo: not run: cancelled in Terminal's password window”.

title: Notifications: a selected card, not an outline
caption: The selected card was drawn with a thick accent outline. Now it sits on a soft tint of the accent with a hairline edge, the way a selected row reads in a list; its text and buttons keep their contrast in light and dark.

title: Selected cards in every look and colour set
caption: The selected Builds card in each of the seven looks, with the BeOS and Catppuccin colour sets in bebox and papercraft, light and dark. The tint comes from each look's own selection colour, so it never fights the yellow window tab.

title: Themes: colour sets selected the same way
caption: Preferences ▸ Themes marks the chosen colour set with the kit's selection plate, the same soft ground as a selected card, in place of a coloured ring.

title: Themes: colour sets selected, dark
caption: The chosen colour set's plate in dark mode.

title: Backgrounds: the chosen wallpaper on a plate
caption: The wallpaper picker (the kit's ThumbnailPicker) shows the chosen picture on a rounded plate a few pixels larger than it, light and dark, rather than a thick border around the picture.

title: Terminal: the group colour you picked
caption: The chosen colour in Name Group is a soft ring around the swatch, in light and dark, instead of a heavy outline.

title: Notification banners: a quieter close box
caption: One close box per banner, in its header beside the app's name, instead of one in the header and another on every notification. In a group of several, each notification shows its own only while the pointer is over it. Both are named buttons in the tree (Close, Close All from Builds), so agents can find them.

title: Notification banners: close box, dark
caption: The same banners in dark mode.

title: Terminal: ⌘ keys as you press them
caption: The Terminal's menus showed ⇧⌘N, ⇧⌘T and so on, because ⌘ reaches a terminal as Ctrl+Shift; they now read ⌘N, ⌘T, as pressed, in the menu bar, context menus and the list agents get. ⌘- and ⌘= (Smaller, Bigger) work now; before, Shift turned - into _ and = into +, and neither matched. A physical Ctrl+Shift+- reaches the shell as Ctrl+_ (readline's undo) instead of being taken for ⌘-: app_server keeps the right Ctrl for ⌘, and the kit tells the two apart in terminal windows.

title: Log Viewer: the detail pane says what it's for
caption: Until you pick a line, the pane under the list was a blank white box. It now says "Select a line to read it whole." in the list's dim empty-state text. This is TextView::empty_text in the kit, the TextView version of ColumnListView::empty_text.

title: Preferences: designed empty states
caption: Before (top) and after, light and dark. A panel with nothing it can show (no sound server, NetworkManager or bluetoothd not running, no fingerprint sensor, no displays) said so in one dim line in the corner of an empty window. The kit's new EmptyState puts the panel's icon and the message in the middle of the space, as lists already do with empty_text.

title: Preferences: Security without the dead band
caption: The Security panel ended in an empty band above Defaults and Revert; the window is now 336 tall (from 354), the least that fits its boxes, so the buttons sit a footer's gap under the last box as in every other panel. Before above, after below, light and dark.

title: Palette: kinds on the line
caption: In Palette results, the kind on the right (Application, File, Web) used to float a few pixels above the name and description beside it. It now sits on the same line, placed with the kit's label_fit, and agents can read it in the tree. Before above, after below.

title: Symbols on the baseline
caption: Symbols Nimbus Sans lacks (the menu-path triangle, arrows, the Command key) come from DejaVu Sans, which egui centred in its own taller line, so they sat a few pixels below the words around them (above: before; below: now). The kit now shifts each fallback face onto the primary face's baseline, so they line up everywhere: Passwords' setup text, Palette's App > Menu paths, shortcuts and prose.

title: History: legible to the last
caption: Notifications in the History window still fade as they age, but never below 30% ink: the oldest note (here 58 minutes old, two minutes from going) is faint but readable, in cards and in lists, instead of nearly invisible while still counted and clickable. Full again when selected or under the pointer.

title: Twitcher: the chosen app on a plate
caption: The app Twitcher has chosen sits on the same rounded selection plate the kit gives a chosen picture (Themes, icon grids), in place of a hard square of menu blue. Its edge colour is now Palette::selection_edge, shared by the kit and app_server.

title: Password alerts sized to their text
caption: The keyring and polkit password alerts are true fixed alerts now, named Authentication in Deskbar, and sized to their own text by the new style::plain_text_height (left: before, a window 18 points too tall; middle: after, dark; right: light, with the mismatch note in the row kept for it). app_server no longer gives a fixed-size window a remembered size from before, and the kit keeps a window within its maximum size.

title: Terminal before: chrome on no common grid
caption: Before: the menu's first title, the side tabs' icons, New Tab and the pane heads' icons each started at a different x; side tabs, top tabs and pane heads were three different heights; the side strip began with a gap under the menu bar, so its top line doubled the bar's.

title: Terminal: chrome on one column and one row
caption: One 12pt left column for the menu's first title, the tab icons, New Tab, the pane heads' icons and the terminal text; one 26pt row for side tabs, top tabs and pane heads, with the 21pt menu bar clearly its own thing; the first side tab hangs from the menu bar (its corner square, the bar's line its top edge). Tiles are laid out in device pixels, so no seams at 1.5x. Reviewed clean by layout_review in light and dark, tabs top and side, tiled and not, at 1x, 1.5x and 2x.

title: Terminal: tabs on top, light, at 1.5x
caption: The same grid with the tabs on top: each tab a pane head's height, standing on the strip's bottom edge, so the selected tab and the pane head under it are one height; icons on the menu's first-title column; one-device-pixel lines and no seams at 1.5x.

title: Date & Time: one baseline for the tabs, the Time field ends with the calendar
caption: Found by the layout review. Every TabView label now sits on one line, the selected tab's too; the Time field sits level with the calendar's sixth week so the two columns end together; the second hand is a device-pixel hairline, so it stays crisp at 1.5x.

title: Text fields: the hint on the label's baseline
caption: Found by the layout review. A TextControl's hint is drawn with the kit's text placement, so it lines up with its label and with typed text at 1x, 1.5x and 2x; it is the field's placeholder for agents too.

title: Menu bar one row with the tabs
caption: The kit's menu bar is 26 points tall, the same row as a tab strip and a pane head, instead of 21 (31.5 device pixels at 1.5x, cramped against the rest). Terminal at 1.5x, tabs down the side.

title: Frames and tabs even at fractional scales
caption: app_server draws the window frame out from where the content lands, in device pixels: outline a hairline, bevel light and shadow a point each rounded, the flat middle taking the rest, the same on all four sides (1, 2, 3, 2 pixels at 1.5x; it was 2, 1, 2, 1, 2 on one side and mirrored differently on the other). Tabs, the wallpaper, the switcher and other app_server pictures are drawn pixel for pixel instead of resampled a pixel off their size. 1.5x, 8x zoom.

title: Terminal: side tabs before
caption: Before: the side strip's tabs ran into the content, the first hung from the menu bar with no room above it, and nothing balanced the left inset on the right.

title: Terminal: side tabs with even room
caption: Side tabs are rounded rows with the same 4-point room on every side: from the window edge, the strip's edge, the menu bar and each other; the selected one is raised in the content's colours. 2x shown; checked at 1x, 1.5x and 2x.

title: Terminal: side tabs beside Show All Tabs
caption: Pane heads beside a side strip are its first tab and the room round it tall (32), so the tab's middle is level with the heads'.

title: Keyboard hints: instant on a busy screen
caption: Control twice now asks only the surfaces showing, for only what can be picked, on worker threads, starting when Control is first let go: the letters show in under a millisecond after the second press (was about half a second, seconds on complex screens).

title: Qt apps before: generic theme
caption: Before: with XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=Olo, Qt didn't know the desktop and took its generic theme, so Ladybird stayed light in its own font while Olo was dark.

title: Qt apps follow Olo: dark
caption: The session now says Olo:GNOME, so Qt takes its GTK 3 theme: Ladybird (from a toolbox) follows Olo's palette, font and light/dark live. 2x shown; checked at 1x, 1.5x and 2x.

title: Qt apps follow Olo: light
caption: The same Ladybird switched back to light live, with no restart.

title: Screen saver: pointer before
caption: Before: started under a still pointer, the screen saver showed the pointer of the window underneath (here a text I-beam) until a move, and a move ends it.

title: Screen saver hides the pointer
caption: app_server hides the pointer while the screen saver runs, from its first frame; the pointer comes back with the first move, which ends it.

title: Noto fonts, shipped with Olo
caption: Before (Nimbus Sans, DejaVu for symbols) above, after (Noto Sans and Noto Sans Mono, with Noto Sans Symbols, Symbols 2 and Math for ⌘ ⌥ arrows and marks) below: one family everywhere, the same on every machine, open and clear at small sizes. app_server's tab titles, Twitcher and hint badges centre their capitals from the face's own metrics.

title: Auto-tiling
caption: Deskbar's tiles beside the cup (or ⌃⌥⌘T) tile every window on the workspace: a new one halves the focused tile along its longer side, a closed one's room goes to its neighbour. Zoom still zooms and comes back; Zoom Vertically makes a column; dialogs and small utility windows such as DeskCalc float; ⌃⌘Z undoes.

title: Deskbar groups applications by workspace
caption: With more than one workspace, Deskbar lists the applications on the workspace showing under its name, and folds the rest under Other Workspaces (BOutlineListView's latch); unfolded, each workspace's under its own heading. Clicking a heading goes there.

title: ⌘Tab keeps to this workspace, ⌥Tab goes everywhere
caption: ⌘Tab (left) switches among this workspace's applications only; ⌥Tab (right) has a numbered row for every workspace with windows, as ⌘Tab had. ⌃Tab is Next Tab in the window.

title: Deskbar's wordmark follows the theme again
caption: Choosing a theme in Preferences drew everything in BeBox: the theme was looked up by its address in THEMES, a const since it moved to olo-theme, so another crate's copy never matched and BeBox (the first) was taken. Now by id; Deskbar's wordmark, every app's icons and Twitcher's follow the theme again (Toybox, Enamel, Halftone, Papercraft, Soft Be, BeBox).

title: Electron windows tile
caption: Slack, and every Electron app, floated over the tiles: Electron sends i32::MAX as its largest size, meaning none, and any largest size floated a window. Now a window floats when it has one size only, or a largest size its display's tiles are bigger than.

title: Deskbar lists every workspace in order, the one showing in a pill
caption: No more Other Workspaces: each workspace with windows gets a quiet caption over its applications, always in ascending order, and the one showing is marked by a pill in the selection's colours (style::selection_ink), so it follows every theme, light and dark. Soft Be, Toybox and Enamel, light and dark, at 2×.

title: Clicking an application in Deskbar brings all its windows
caption: A left click on StyledEdit (left) brings both its windows forward, the minimized one too, with the last one used in front and focused (right), as the Dock does; a right click still lists the windows to choose one.

title: ⌥Tab keeps to this workspace, ⌘Tab goes everywhere, and Deskbar follows
caption: Reversing the earlier swap: ⌘Tab's Twitcher shows every workspace's applications, ⌥Tab only this one's. While it's up, Deskbar highlights the application Twitcher is on (style::selection_wash), here DeskCalc.

title: Deskbar lights the workspace showing
caption: The whole workspace showing, its heading and its applications, is washed in the selection's colour across the bar with a hairline of the selection's edge above and below, like a BListView selection as big as the group; the other workspaces stay on the plain panel. Its heading takes the selection's text colour, and its rows shade that ground for focus, hover and separators, so it follows every theme and colour set, light, dark and night. Twitcher's choice inside it takes the menu's stronger selection so it still stands out. Light and dark at 2×.

title: StyledEdit on the kit's text editor
caption: StyledEdit now draws with olo_kit::editor, one laid-out paragraph each, so a long document types and scrolls inside a frame. Left, centred, right and justified text keep their edges on the margin, trailing spaces and all.

title: StyledEdit keeps its place through an upgrade
caption: After an in-place reload StyledEdit comes back scrolled where it was, with its caret, its selection and any unsaved edits (here line 614, edited).

title: Read-only documents grey out their Font menu
caption: A file you can't write opens read-only: Font and Document's commands are disabled, and so are their submenus, rather than doing nothing when chosen.

title: Notifications: times sit on the title's baseline
caption: The app and time line up with the title's baseline rather than its box, and rows land on whole device pixels at 1.5× too.

title: Tracker's item count lines up with its list
caption: The count bar's text starts in line with the list's icons above it (here at 1× and 2×), and the free space keeps the same inset from the right.

title: Themes: before, the colour schemes ran into the buttons
caption: At 1x the panel's fixed height was too short for the colour-scheme cards: BeOS's description ran onto three lines and pushed under Defaults and Revert.

title: Themes: after, every card fits
caption: Preferences panels are sized for their tallest content (Themes 560x634, Display 500x490, Keyboard 480x736, Touchpad 460x586, About 444x290), checked at 1x, 1.5x and 2x, light and dark. Power and Security's menus share widgets::divider_for, the widest label and the gap after it, so the wells line up and every label fits.

title: Menu shortcuts: ⇧ stands with the capitals
caption: Noto Sans Symbols puts ⇧ a device pixel below the capitals at every scale. key_combo now places a symbol about as tall as the capitals by its ink, so the feet of ⇧⌘Z line up at 1x, 1.25x, 1.5x, 1.75x and 2x.

title: Terminal shows its tab strip with one tab
caption: The tab strip no longer waits for a second tab: one tab shows with its icon, title, close box and +, so a new tab is always a click away (light and dark at 1×, 1.5× and 2×).

title: Screenshot's caption lines up with Save as
caption: The caption under the preview sits level with the Save as: row beside it at 1×, 1.5× and 2×, in light, dark and night.

title: Disk Usage: crisp hairlines and bars at 1.5×
caption: The lines between slices, round each ring and round the hub are one device pixel at every scale (style::hairline), and the bars' widths land on whole device pixels, so at 1.5× nothing is blurred across two.

title: Deskbar's badge ring is one device pixel
caption: The panel-coloured ring that cuts the unread badge out of the bell is a whole device pixel wide at 1.5× too, rather than a blurred pixel and a half.

title: The overview, on ⌃Space
caption: Every workspace at once, a pane each, its windows spread out live and lettered: click one or type its letter to go to it, the arrows and Return walk them, Esc leaves. Windows showing glide into place and back; the rest fade in.

title: Spotlight while switching
caption: While ⌘Tab is held, every window but the chosen app's dims, so the one you're about to switch to stands out; it follows each step and fades back when you let go or cancel.

title: Terminal comes back after the session ends
caption: When the session ends, olo-termd keeps each shell's lines. Terminal remembers its windows and tabs, so the next login puts each tab back in its folder, with what it showed and a dim "Restored from" line.

title: Approve Without Asking
caption: Deskbar's new key in the tray turns on approving without asking for a while: sudo in Terminal and Passwords' unlock and op go ahead without a window, each in a quiet notification. It takes the account password and ends at its time or when the screen locks.

title: The key's tip, past Deskbar's edge
caption: While on, the key is gold and its tip says how long is left. Tray tips now show in a popup of their own (olo_kit::tip), so they reach past Deskbar's narrow window instead of being cut.

title: Terminal's sudo window shows the whole command
caption: A command too long for the window is elided in the field; resting on it shows the whole command in a kit tip that extends past the window (egui's own was cut at its edge).

title: Focus mode
caption: A new windowing mode: only the active window shows, zoomed, with its app's other windows as tabs along the top and its dialogs and panels over it. Activating another window (Deskbar, ⌘Tab, the overview) shows that one instead.

title: Choose the windowing mode from the tray
caption: Deskbar's tray icon is now the windowing mode (Standard, Auto-Tiling or Focus) of this workspace on this display: either click opens the modes, then the arranging commands. ⌃⌥⌘T and ⌃⌥⌘O toggle Auto-Tiling and Focus.

title: Default windowing mode in Preferences
caption: Preferences ▸ Windows chooses the mode a workspace starts in; Deskbar's tray chooses each workspace's own.

title: Deskbar: every display's own workspaces
caption: Each display has its own workspaces and its own Deskbar, listing only its workspaces, headed D0/D1/D2 Workspace N; the windowing mode moved from the tray to each heading's right end (D2's is Auto-Tiling here).

title: Deskbar: a workspace heading's menu
caption: Right-clicking a heading: Show, Hide or Close All of its windows, move them to the same workspace of another display, or to any workspace of any display.

title: Twitcher: displays numbered
caption: Columns are displays (D0, D1, D2 and their names), rows workspace numbers: a cell is that display's workspace.

title: Deskbar: tray icons in even rows
caption: More icons than fit go into as many rows as needed, shared out evenly (eight are two rows of four), at 1x, 1.5x and 2x, light and dark.

title: Preferences: workspaces are per display
caption: The Workspaces panel says each display has its own; Displays has no Deskbar-on-every-display setting any more.

title: Keyboard Shortcuts sheet (⇧⌘/)
caption: Every shortcut of the keyboard profile on one sheet: the front app's menu keys first (Tracker's here), then text editing's and the desktop's, as cards in columns; ⇧⌘/ on a Mac, Win+Shift+/ on Windows, Alt+Shift+/ on BeOS.

title: Keyboard profiles in Preferences
caption: Preferences ▸ Keyboard ▸ Shortcuts picks a keyboard profile (Mac, Windows, BeOS, or one saved) with its command key and key behaviour, then lists every shortcut in the platform's own key names (here Windows': Win+← snaps left); a change makes it “Windows (Customized)”.

title: Menus in the profile's keys (Windows)
caption: Every app's menu keys come from the keyboard profile: with Windows' keys Tracker's File menu has Explorer's (Alt+↑, Alt+Enter, F2, Del, Ctrl+Shift+N); with a Mac's, Finder's (⌘↑, ⌘I, ⇧⌘N, ⌘⌫).

title: Notifications: pin and snooze
caption: A right click on a note (in the History, or on a banner) pins it or snoozes it; Edit has the same for the selected note. Pinned notes never fade, survive Clear All and Close All, and their banners stay on screen until closed, even across a restart. Snoozed ones go away and come back as new after 15 minutes, an hour, three hours or at nine tomorrow morning.

title: A pinned banner says so
caption: The header of a banner whose notes are all pinned reads Pinned beside its close box; the history adds Pinned after a note's time.

title: Quick Look: Markdown as a set page
caption: Markdown in Quick Look reads like a well-set page: a measure of at most 680 points, a 20-point line, headings with room above and rules under the first two, hanging indents with lined-up numbers and real task boxes, GitHub's alerts, and code coloured by its language.

title: Quick Look: tables, pictures and links
caption: Tables are as wide as what they hold and line up as the Markdown says; the document's own pictures show, crisp; links open, and a #heading link scrolls to it. Long documents lay out a few milliseconds a frame, so nothing waits.

title: Quick Look: search, sort and scroll tables
caption: CSV and spreadsheets in Quick Look scroll sideways to every column, take the first row as the columns' names, line numbers up on the right, keep only the rows a search finds (in every column or one) and sort by a header click, numbers as numbers. Big sheets are searched and sorted on a worker.

title: Terminal: repositories, worktrees and pull requests
caption: A window whose tabs are all in one git repository becomes its group on its own; the group's menu lists the repository's worktrees and makes new ones; a tab on a branch with a pull request on GitHub wears GitHub's mark in the state's colour, its commit filled as its checks pass, fail or run (here: open, checks running).

title: Terminal: New Worktree…
caption: The group's New Worktree… (also Tabs ▸ Repository): a name that is a folder and a branch both, made in Preferences ▸ Terminal's location; the note says where it goes and on which branch (or, in red, why not), as you type. Files check out on a thread with progress and Stop.

title: Preferences ▸ Terminal (light)
caption: A new panel: where New Worktree… makes a repository's worktrees, ~/worktrees to start, each repository a folder of its name in there. Terminal follows it live.

title: Preferences ▸ Terminal (dark)
caption: The same panel in dark mode.

title: Terminal: tab groups in a window
caption: Several groups per window, as a browser's: each run led by a chip with its name in its colour and a line of it over its tabs. Tabs join and leave by dragging; a chip drags its whole group; a tab or group dragged out of the strip becomes a window under the pointer.

title: Terminal: tab groups down the side
caption: Down the side, each group's chip heads its tabs with a bar of its colour beside them.

title: Terminal: side tabs as Deskbar's list
caption: Tabs down the side are Deskbar's rows now: the panel's ground, a hairline under each, the one showing recessed, groups under small bold headings with a dot of their colour and a bar of it down the left. Show All Tabs' pane heads are tinted with their group's colour, a line of it across the top. (1.5×, light.)

title: Terminal: quiet group chips along the top
caption: Along the top, a group's chip is a dot of its colour and its name in quiet bold, no pill, with the line of its colour over its tabs; pane heads take the group's colour too. (1×, night.)

title: Preferences: Integrations
caption: A panel for every service Olo works with, each with its own icon: GitHub shows whom Olo is connected as and from where (a token kept by Olo, GH_TOKEN, or the GitHub CLI's sign-in, now read from the login keyring too), and connects with a token. Terminal's pull requests use it.

title: Icons: Integrations, GitHub, Chrome and Slack
caption: Olo's own takes on GitHub's, Chrome's and Slack's marks (and Integrations' puzzle pieces), in every theme; Chrome's and Slack's replace the icons those programs ship wherever Olo shows them.

title: Passwords: search with filters
caption: The search field colours filters and suggests them as you type (has:we → Website, Weak Password, with counts); a filter bar over the list (Tag, Has) edits the same query. Words find usernames and non-secret fields of every item, best matches first, marked in the rows.

title: Passwords: search, dark
caption: A left-out filter (-has:reused) in red; matches marked.

title: Filter menus with counts
caption: A filter's menu: Any, then each value with how many items have it, where a shortcut would be.

title: Log Viewer: one search, filters as menus
caption: The search takes words, phrases, -words and program:/level:/since:/pid: filters (several programs at once, all, or one left out), with Program, Level and Time menus beside it editing the same text; what was found is marked in the messages.

title: Log Viewer: narrow, dark
caption: In a narrow window the menus go under the search, their text over the list's first column.

title: Terminal: smaller pull request marks in the tab strip
caption: Before (left) and after at 2×. The pull request mark is drawn as big as the text (12 pt, from GitHub's 16-unit drawing, its lines whole device pixels at every scale) and sits in the close box's place, which takes it over only under the pointer, so titles get the room back and nothing moves; each group's colour bar stops short of the next group's.

title: Passwords: passkeys in Chrome
caption: Passwords is Chrome's passkey authenticator: it asks in an alert in front which account to sign in with (a choice when there are several, Use Another Device… for Chrome's own QR-code sheet), and a sign-in that suggests passkeys has Olo ▸ Sign In with Passkey in the field's menu. At 2×; reviewed at 1×, 1.5× and 2×.

title: Auto-tiling: every window fits where an arrangement lets it
caption: Before (left): five windows opened in turn under auto-tiling on a 1440×900 display, the fifth (Passwords) halving a tile too small for it, overlapping three. After (right): the tree arranged again so each window has its least size: Disk Usage over Log Viewer, Passwords over StyledEdit and Activity Monitor.

title: Quick Look: TOML (and INI) highlighted
caption: TOML files (and Cargo.lock, uv.lock, poetry.lock) are coloured by a grammar of Quick Look's own: tables as headings, keys, strings of every kind, numbers, booleans and dates, arrays and inline tables; INI-style files (systemd units, .desktop entries, git config) by another. Light and dark, at 2×.

title: Tracker: Column View keeps its highlight
caption: → into a folder highlights its first item again. A selection put back after an upgrade waited for items that never came, and wiped the active column's selection each time a listing landed; now a waiting selection belongs to its own folder only, and the window comes back with its columns. → before a listing lands selects once it does, and a selection made in code scrolls into view in every view.

title: Deskbar: a dot for apps with notifications
caption: An application with notifications unread has a quiet dot at the right of its Deskbar row, in the colour the history marks unread ones with (not an alarm's red); a new one arriving shakes it gently side to side, unless Do Not Disturb is on. Agents read the row's value, "has notifications".

title: Agent Screens: History and Replay
caption: Each agent screen keeps what was done on it and the frames it drew. History lists the actions (searchable), shows the screen as it was at the one chosen, and plays it back in time with them: clicks as rings, keys as captions, quiet stretches skipped. Export Video… makes it an MP4 in process. Stopped screens' histories stay listed, by last use; how much is kept is in Preferences ▸ AI.

title: Share Screen: the screen-sharing picker
caption: olo-portal's picker when an app asks to share the screen (xdg-desktop-portal ScreenCast): who asks, the screens as live thumbnails shaped like them, Cancel / Share. A fixed kit dialog opened over the asking window.

title: Deskbar: what is being shared, with Stop Sharing
caption: While an app shares a screen, Deskbar's tray shows a screen with a recording's red dot; its menu says what is shared with whom and stops it (the app is told the share closed).

title: Share Screen: screens and windows
caption: The screen-sharing picker offers windows too (what the app asked for): Screens and Windows, each a live thumbnail; a window is shared as only what its client draws, at its own size.

title: Permission: the portals' dialog as an Olo alert
