caption: olo-portal answers the Access portal, which other portals ask permission through (a camera, a screenshot): Olo's BAlert with the portal's icon, its question and its choices.

title: Open and Save for other programs: Olo's file panel
caption: olo-portal answers the FileChooser portal: another program's Open or Save is Olo's file panel, titled as it asks, in its folder, filtered to its file types.

title: File panel: filters, several files, an app's choices
caption: Other programs' Open dialogs (the FileChooser portal) now show the app's filters as a Show pop-up (by glob or MIME type), choose several files with ⇧ and ⌘ clicks, and carry the app's own choices above the buttons, the pop-ups lined up on one divider. Chrome's multi-file uploads come back whole.

title: Open With: other programs' app chooser
caption: When an app opens a file or link through the OpenURI portal and the handler isn't settled, Olo's own Open With window asks (the AppChooser portal): what is opened, the apps that handle it with their icons and kinds, the last choice selected, the keyboard in the list.

title: Deskbar: other programs' tray icons
caption: Slack's, Discord's, Telegram's tray icons (StatusNotifierItem) now sit in Deskbar's tray with Olo's own: their pictures drawn a texel to a device pixel at every scale, their tips (named by the program when they give no title), and their menus as Olo menus, read ahead so they open at once.

title: Deskbar: programs' unread badges and progress
caption: A program's launcher badge (Slack's unread count, Chrome's download progress) lights its row's quiet dot, shaking it when the count rises, and its progress runs as a thin bar along the row's foot.

title: Portal: Set as Desktop Background
caption: Other programs' Set as Desktop Background (the Wallpaper portal) asks with the picture, as a BAlert, and sets it as Preferences would; the Screenshot portal's PickColor freezes the screen with a loupe; Send by Email opens a mailto: link.

title: Screenshot: pick a colour
caption: PickColor (for other programs, through the Screenshot portal): the screen frozen, a loupe by the pointer with the pixels around it magnified, the one under it ringed, its swatch and hex.

title: Portal: other programs' global shortcuts
caption: An app's keys that work whatever has the keyboard (push-to-talk) are asked for once, listing each and its keys; ones Olo already has show as in use. Allowed ones are held by app_server for the app, through upgrades.

title: Activity Monitor: sections, cards and live graphs
caption: A sidebar of sections (Overview, Processes, CPU, Memory, Disks, Network, GPU, Sensors, System, Graphs), each figure live in the sidebar; the Overview's cards lead into each section, and clicking a graph shows what was busiest at that moment. Graphs scroll a device pixel at a time; built from the kit's new Sidebar, dashboard and Graph.

title: Activity Monitor: the CPU, dark
caption: Each core with its frequency, each cluster's governor, where idle time goes (WFI, powered down) and the load.

title: Activity Monitor: every process, as a list or a tree
caption: Searched and filtered with the kit's search (user:, state:, kind:, pid:), sorted by any of twelve columns (names in natural order), as a tree of who started whom (kernel threads folded here). Double-click or ⌘I for its inspector: threads, open files, memory, environment, cores, limits, priority and signals.

title: Downloads in Tracker, as they will be
caption: A download Chrome is writing (NAME.crdownload) shows in Tracker under the name it will have, with its kind's icon, how far along it is (a bar under its icon; '3.1 of 10 MB' and 'Downloading, 31%' in the list and preview), from the size olo-chrome marks it with (user.olo.expected_size).

title: Activity Monitor: programs using the network
caption: Each process's TCP traffic, from netlink's sock_diag (tcp_info's byte counts) summed by the sockets' owners: a card in the Network section and Sent and Received columns in the process list. Connections and interface counters come from netlink too.

title: Alerts open in the middle of the screen, in front
caption: An alert asked for where no window of its app has the focus (Empty Trash from the desktop's Trash icon) opened in the next cascade slot, at the top left of some display, where it went unseen. Now it opens in the middle of the display the pointer is on, in front and focused, and stays over its app's windows until answered.

title: Deskbar's notification dot drains as they fade
caption: An app's dot in Deskbar is filled from the left to how fresh its notifications are together (each 1/n, as the history fades them), never below a third, the rest a faint well of its colour; with Preferences ▸ Notifications ▸ Show how many beside each app's dot, the count beside it (here 2, partway through a 2-minute fade, at 2×).

title: Notifications: All Apps, mixed while they differ
caption: Preferences ▸ Notifications' Applications table has an All Apps row over the list: each column checked when every app's is, a dash while they differ (the kit's CheckBox::mixed); a click sets it for every app. With the Deskbar box above it, the panel is taller.

title: New windows glow a moment (Preferences ▸ Appearance)
caption: With Glow new windows for N seconds on (off by default, 5 s), a new window has a soft halo in the look's focus blue round its frame and tab as one shape, fading out over its last second; left: just opened, right: after (at 1×, enlarged 2×).

title: Token Pool: the Clients window
caption: Pool ▸ Clients: the pool's activity over time (requests a minute by client, over the last hour, six hours or day, with totals), Codex's service with its version, settings, connections, conversations and Restart, and each Claude Code and Codex running and where its connections go (here a sandbox with a made-up day of activity).

title: Window menu: every display's workspaces
caption: A window's tab menu ▸ Move to Workspace lists every display's workspaces, left to right as Deskbar names them, its own display's with their keys and a check; another display's moves it there, to the same place, tiled or zoomed as it was.

title: Deskbar: an app's windows to any workspace
caption: An app's Deskbar menu moves its windows as a tab's menu moves one: Move to Workspace ▸ every display's workspaces (the one they're on checked), and To the Next / Previous Display.

title: Deskbar: every display's workspaces, and the display's number
caption: Each Deskbar lists every display's workspaces and their apps, its own display's first (here D1's Deskbar, then D0's), and its tray shows its display's number in a small monitor; clicking it lists the displays and goes to the one chosen.

title: Terminal: Tile All Tabs, a row per group
caption: Tile All Tabs (was Show All Tabs) gives each group a row, its tabs side by side, and the ungrouped tabs a row of their own; clicking groups' chips chooses which tile (lit as Deskbar's workspace showing): here alpha and beta of three, a row each; one alone fills a grid; the right button gives the group's menu.

title: Preferences ▸ Terminal: Coding Agents
caption: Tell coding agents about the repositories in their tab group (off by default): Claude Code and Codex in a tab of a group spanning repositories are told the group's name and its repositories and worktrees, through their own hooks.

title: Notifications: only the latest of the same
caption: Preferences ▸ Notifications ▸ History: Only the latest of the same notification (on by default): the same again from the same app takes the earlier one's place while it's still showing or unread.

title: Agent Screens: History follows the agent live
caption: Agent Screens revamped: a sidebar of running and stopped screens, a header saying how the chosen one is, and Live, History and Stats tabs. History now follows the history as it's written (each new action chosen and shown as it comes), its scroll bar works (the list was pinned to the playhead's row every frame), and a search with Kind, Result and Time filters narrows it; under the picture, what the action did.

title: Agent Screens: filters
caption: History's filters, as Log Viewer's: Result ▸ Failed keeps the 12 of 249 actions that failed, each with why in red.

title: Agent Screens: Stats
caption: Stats as dashboard cards (dark, 1.5×): use, actions by kind, actions a minute over the last hour, programs run.

title: Terminal: Tile All Tabs rows' heights dragged
caption: In Tile All Tabs, the line between two groups' rows (and the heads under it) drags their heights; the shares go by group and are kept with the window. The right button there gives the group's menu with Reset Row Heights.

title: Performance supervisor: Activity Monitor's Supervisor section and Preferences ▸ Performance
caption: The supervisor (off by default) lowers builds and background work and watches for stuck processes, leaks, memory hogs and zombies, each judged from several signals with a confidence and evidence. Activity Monitor shows it as cards (Inspect, Stop Process, Ignore This Process); every threshold is tuned in Preferences ▸ Performance.

title: Performance supervisor, dark
caption: The same in the dark look: the findings' confidence in the failure colour.

title: Supervisor alert, sized for its buttons
caption: An urgent finding asks in an alert naming the process, what was found and the evidence. The kit's WindowOptions::alert_buttons widens an alert to fit long button labels.

title: Inspector: the Supervisor tab
caption: A process's inspector has a Supervisor tab: its findings, how sure and why, and whether it was lowered and why. The alert's Show in Activity Monitor opens it there.

title: Deskbar: the supervisor's gauge at 1×, 1.25×, 1.5×, 1.75×, 2×
caption: On (dial tinted, needle up, the findings counted, red if urgent) and off (dim, needle resting). A click turns it on or off; its menu lists the findings, Show in Activity Monitor and Performance Settings…

title: Terminal: a coding agent's title for its tab
caption: With Preferences ▸ Terminal's new setting, Claude Code and Codex get a set_tab_title tool (an MCP server of Terminal's) and are asked to keep their tab titled with what they're working on; here the tool was called from the tab.

title: Preferences ▸ Terminal: Let coding agents keep their tab's title current
caption: Off by default; the panel is taller for it.

title: Quick Look full screen on two displays: before
caption: Quick Look on the right display, F: it filled the left display (the first one), and on the right it hung off its old place at full-screen size.

title: Quick Look full screen on two displays: after
caption: F fills only the display the window is on; the other is untouched, and F again puts it back where it was. Same at 1.5× and 2×.

title: StyledEdit: paragraph styles and lists
caption: Paragraphs have a style (Title, Heading 1-3, Quote, Code, Body), bulleted and numbered lists that nest and number themselves, indents and their own alignment; the kit's editor sets each paragraph's indents, spacing and list marker (Document::paragraph). Word count in the status line.

title: StyledEdit: spelling as you type
caption: Misspelled words get a red wave under them (the kit editor's Options::spelling, Hunspell dictionaries read natively by spellbook); right-click one for suggestions, Ignore Spelling or Learn Spelling.

title: Printing: the Print panel and PDF
caption: StyledEdit's File > Print... (and Export > PDF): a printer from CUPS (spoken to natively over IPP) or a PDF, paper, copies and pages; pages laid out as the editor lays them out and made into a PDF in process (krilla), fonts embedded, text selectable.

title: StyledEdit: tables
caption: A paragraph can be a table's row: its cells its text between tabs, laid out side by side in columns by the kit editor and ruled a device pixel wide (a header row shaded). Tab and ⇧Tab go from cell to cell, Tab in the last cell and Return add a row, and edits keep a table's cells and rows. The Table menu inserts and converts tables, adds and deletes rows and columns, and toggles the header; Word, OpenDocument, RTF and Markdown tables come in as tables and go out as them.

title: File panels: Kind column, sorting, Favorites and Recent Folders
caption: Every Open and Save panel lists Name, Kind, Size and Modified, sorted by any of them (folders first, names in natural order); the folder pop-up has the folders above this one, the standard places, Favorites (add or remove this folder) and Recent Folders, kept in ~/.config/olo/places.json and shared with Tracker's Go menu. Space looks at the selected file in the Viewer, as Quick Look.

title: StyledEdit: dragging a table's column rule
caption: A table's inner rule can be dragged: a line shows where it will go, and let go, every row of the table takes the new widths (one step to undo). The widths are kept in StyledEdit's own files and in Word, OpenDocument, RTF and HTML.

title: StyledEdit: the ruler, indents and tab stops
caption: A ruler over the text (the kit's ruler; Document ▸ Show Ruler): the caret's paragraph's first-line, left and right indents to drag, and tab stops: a click sets one, a drag moves it or takes it off, and its menu (or a double click) makes it left, centre, right or decimal. Tabs now go to stops (epaint's TabStops); here a left stop at 1½ in and a decimal one at 2¼ in line up a price list. Indents and stops are kept in Word, OpenDocument and RTF.

title: StyledEdit: Header & Footer
caption: Document ▸ Header & Footer… sets a left, centre and right part above and below every printed page, {page} and {pages} standing for the page number and count. Kept in the file, and in Word, OpenDocument and RTF (checked in LibreOffice).

title: StyledEdit: pictures
caption: Pictures in the text: Insert Picture…, pasted or dropped; drawn by the kit's editor where their character is, sized from the Edit menu, kept beside the document, and in Word, OpenDocument, RTF, web pages, Markdown and print.

title: StyledEdit: Page View
caption: Document ▸ Page View sets the text on sheets of the paper it prints on, with its margins: paragraphs and rows break across pages as printed, headers and footers on each sheet; the kit editor's Options::pages.

title: StyledEdit: Page View, dark
caption: The desk half way to black under dark sheets.

title: Telegram: polls and reactions on their baselines
caption: A poll's shares stand on their answers' baseline; a reaction's count is centred in its chip by its figures with the emoji on their middle, and the emoji lines up with the message text above. Voice notes' waveform bars and the file glyph sit on device pixels at every scale. The layout review now judges an emoji inside a line of text with that line, not against the whole bubble.

title: Preferences ▸ Display: each display's panel
caption: What the display is (make, size, density, refresh), what Olo works out about its panel (technology, colour stripes) and how it draws text on it, with why, each correctable (Automatic or a choice). Shown on a simulated 24-inch 1080p LCD (92 ppi): subpixel text.

title: GPUI kit: the column list view
caption: olo-ui gains BColumnListView (right), as the egui kit draws it (left, the demo's Lists tab): header sorting and dividers, the file-manager selection (shared now as olo_kit_base::list), bands, type-select, BeOS scroll bars; at 1.5x, where GPUI windows had been drawn at 2x and shrunk (fixed here).

title: Token Pool on GPUI
caption: Token Pool moves to olo-ui: the same window (gateway, now-grid, client switches, account cards with quota bars and request strips, Account menu, rename), drawn by GPUI. A test account in a fixture home; 73.6 MB against egui's 91.9 MB, idle with no wakeups.

title: DiskUsage on GPUI
caption: DiskUsage moves to the GPUI kit (olo-ui): the ring chart's slices are GPU sectors (paint_sector) with hairlines over them, the list beside it a ColumnListView whose rows drag into the Collector, Volumes, menus with the keyboard profile's keys, alerts and the folder panel all as before. The chart redraws only when the slice under the pointer changes, in about a millisecond; the list's name column now fits inside its scroll bar (egui's cut Files off), and the Collector's chips show each file's kind.

title: Screenshot on GPUI
caption: Screenshot moves to the GPUI kit: the same form and buttons, the preview made at exactly its frame's size in device pixels (remade when the scale changes) and drawn one pixel to a pixel, Copy to clipboard as image/png through GPUI's clipboard (which now offers images and data, not only text), Save closing the window and holding the path on the clipboard until something else is copied. The ⌘⇧4 region picker and the colour picker are GPUI layer overlays showing each output's frozen picture 1:1.

title: DriveSetup on GPUI
caption: DriveSetup moves to the GPUI kit: the disk map (segments to scale, hatched free space, the unlocked contents under a purple band) over the list of disks and volumes, the status line with progress and Stop, and its forms (Format, Create with a size slider, Resize, Rename, Unlock, New Partition Table) as alert windows that grow and shrink with their fields. Here on the test UDisks (udisks-fake). The kit gains BeOS keyboard navigation for it: Tab moves through fields, lists and controls (the focused control's label underlined in blue, Space presses it), and a default button answers Return from anywhere in its window.

title: The command palette on GPUI
caption: The command palette, its window menu and the shortcuts sheet move to the GPUI kit. Same look; key symbols (⇧ ⌘ ↵) set on the capitals' line by their outlines, the subtitle and kind on the title's baseline, the query lined up with the titles. It opens in 28 ms (egui: 47) and holds 40 MB less; small text's darkening is now an emboldened outline rather than a stroke (the same look, a third of the time).

title: Log Viewer on GPUI
caption: Log Viewer moves to the GPUI kit, with the kit's new search field (filters coloured, suggested as they're typed), filter bar and text view; the Message column now fits beside the scroll bar (no sideways scrolling). Loading 160,000 lines its slowest frame is 3 ms (egui's 34). A made-up log file, not a real journal.

title: Google Chrome's installer on GPUI
caption: The offer to download Google Chrome (shown when it isn't installed) moves to the GPUI kit, now with its installer icon, which the egui window never found. 54 MB against 77.

title: Deskbar on GPUI
caption: Deskbar moves to Olo's GPUI kit: the same tile, tray and workspaces, drawn on device pixels at every scale (the tray's glyphs as exact paths and GPU arcs), its menus' keys laid out as the egui kit's key combos, tips in popups of their own, applications dragged out as links with their icon and name. 57 MB against 141, and 32 frames for 30 pointer moves against 150.

title: Telegram on GPUI
caption: Telegram moves to the GPUI kit: the same list, conversation and composer (a multi-line field: Return sends, Shift-Return a new line), its panes cached views of their own so a hover, a scroll or the caret redraws only its pane. Shown: the demo account's forum with topics, a reply, code and a photo, at 2x.

title: Menus without stray separators
caption: A menu built with items it shows only sometimes (Telegram's Chat menu with no chat open) ended in a separator with nothing under it; the GPUI kit now leaves out separators at either end of a menu and two together.

title: Viewer on GPUI
caption: The Viewer moved to the GPUI kit: pictures fitted and resampled exactly to the device size on a worker, zoomed in tiles; the crop frame drawn over the picture, its thirds while it moves and its size under it; PDF forms, text boxes, ink and signatures; formatted documents, sheets, code, archives, fonts, sound and video from olo-preview's GPUI views. Windows open sized for the display they open on.

title: Notifications on GPUI
caption: Notifications, banners and History, now on Olo's GPUI: the same cards, groups, stop signs, balloons and reply fields, with words kept on a row when they fit (spaces hang past the edge, as egui and typesetters wrap), the generic application icon for apps without one in banners and History alike, and an exact gap after an error's stop sign. 61 MB against egui's 153 with four banners; History scrolls 200 notes at 1.3–1.8 ms a frame.

title: The share picker on GPUI
caption: olo-portal's dialogs move to the GPUI kit: the share picker (live thumbnails in the kit's new ThumbnailPicker), permission, wallpaper, shortcuts and Open With questions, and the file and Print panels, each over the asking app's window by xdg-foreign. Its thumbnails no longer pile up in the GPU's atlas; a permission dialog opens in ~8 ms.

title: Agent Screens on GPUI
caption: Agent Screens moved to Olo's GPUI: the sidebar, header and Live/History/Stats tabs as before, now with the kit's GPUI Sidebar, TabView and dashboard cards. Live takes a picture only when the screen draws something new (app_server's new Painted event), each resampled to the exact device size on a worker; History plays back drawing only what changes.

title: Activity Monitor on GPUI
caption: Activity Monitor moves from egui to Olo's GPUI kit, looking as it did. Its window is cached parts with the section's graphs on a layer of their own (the kit's GraphLayer): a graph moving a pixel redraws the graphs, not the cards around them. Graphs' fills are a new GPU primitive (paint_area) instead of paths filled through window-sized multisampled textures, and a window's graphs move together on one clock. On release at 2×: the UI thread at or under egui's in every section with graphs (CPU 3.9% of a core against 5.2), 93–96 MB against 119–123.

title: Passwords on GPUI
caption: Passwords moves to the GPUI kit: its panes are cached parts of the window, so a one-time code counting down redraws the item pane alone, once a second; half the CPU of the egui version in every interaction and 90 MB against 124. Synthetic items from the test 1Password.

title: Activity Monitor ▸ Displays
caption: Each display's frames a second, the ones dropped (a vblank or more late), what its frames cost app_server to draw and how app_server paces them (frames.rs: the draw's share of the frame set from its cost and from drops), whether the pointer is on a plane of its own; and the check box that has every drop logged with what went into it. Made-up displays here (OLO_ACTIVITY_DEMO_FRAMES); a headless session has none.

title: Olo Doctor
caption: A new app that looks the computer over for what gets in Olo's way (an input remapper grabbing the mice, USB receivers allowed to sleep, Olo's udev rules missing, rtkit down, another desktop's daemons, programs on an old version) and fixes each with a button, or all at once with one password.

title: Mice by make and model
caption: Preferences ▸ Touchpad & Mouse ▸ Mouse names each mouse by maker and model (sensor, resolution, how it's connected), offers the profile recommended for it or settings of its own, says what is known about it, and points at Olo Doctor for what gets in its way (a key remapper grabbing it, a receiver allowed to sleep). The device list now comes by event, not every 3 s.

title: Screen saver on GPUI
caption: olo-screensaver draws on Olo's GPUI: Message, Icons, Lissart, Lens and Spots (rows) at 1, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75 and 2× (columns), over a test desktop. Lens magnifies the desktop through textured triangles, Lissart's hundreds of lines are painted a layer at a time.

title: StyledEdit on GPUI
caption: StyledEdit moves to the GPUI kit: its editor, ruler and spelling are olo-ui's now. Page View with a header, a table and a picture at 2x. Scrolls, types and resizes within a 120 Hz frame at every scale on a full 16-inch screen, as evenly as egui did; ends stretch and spring back.

title: Tracker on GPUI
caption: Tracker moved from the egui kit to Olo's GPUI: folder windows (icons, mini icons, list, columns), the desktop, Get Info, Find, Tracker Status and Quick Look, with BeOS's drag rules through GPUI's own drops and Paste read off the UI thread.

title: Pinch to zoom, off by default
caption: Preferences ▸ Touchpad & Mouse ▸ Gestures: a pinch reaches the window under the pointer only when this is on. Off, two fingers drifting together while scrolling no longer zoom Chrome's pages.

title: Preferences on GPUI
caption: Every panel of Preferences moved from egui to Olo's GPUI, drawn as before; Themes shows each theme's wordmark and icons, and its colour sets now share their row evenly.

title: Terminal's tabs, redesigned
caption: Terminal on GPUI with a new tab strip (olo-ui's TabStrip): everything sits inside the band. Tabs are their titles; the selected one is on a raised plate lit from above (a touch lighter at the top, its rim's top edge lit and tapering into the corners, a soft shadow), as BeOS lit its controls. A group is a capsule of its colour around its chip and tabs, with corners concentric with the plates inside. No lines, and nothing rises above the strip. Each tab is as wide as its title needs.

title: Terminal's tabs in light mode
caption: The same strip in light mode: a white plate on the quiet band, each group's capsule at 16% of its colour (22% in the dark).

title: Terminal's Tile All Tabs heads
caption: In Tile All Tabs each pane's head is on the strip's quiet band, with its group's chip at the right instead of a tint and a coloured line. The pane you type in has its title in full ink and medium weight, like the strip's selected tab. Icon, title and chip are centred on the band to the device pixel at every scale.

title: Picture in picture stays in its corner
caption: A call popped out of Chrome (documentPictureInPicture, as Meet does) opens in the bottom right corner at its own size, over every window and on each workspace, out of Chrome's group, Focus's zoom and the window memory; the keyboard stays where it was. A link opened from another app (Terminal's Open Pull Request) now shows in Chrome, in front, with the call over it: before, the call joined Chrome's group and zoomed over the tab the link had opened in.

title: A video's picture in picture, Standard mode
caption: Chrome's video picture in picture (no app id, titled "Picture in picture") in the corner, 16 px in, over the call page's window.

title: AirPods panel
caption: Preferences ▸ AirPods: levels with a picture of each bud and the case, noise control with Adaptive's strength, press and hold, listening features, the microphone, and what this computer does with them. Shown with a pretend pair (OLO_FAKE_AIRPODS).

title: AirPods panel, dark, 1×
caption: The same at 1× in dark mode.

title: Sound: AirPods
caption: Preferences ▸ Sound with AirPods as the output: their model, codec and whether they play at music or call quality, noise control, and where to record from while they're connected.

title: Deskbar: AirPods
caption: Deskbar's tray shows AirPods while they're connected (amber or red when a bud runs low); its menu has their levels, noise control, Conversation Awareness and their settings.

title: AirPods icons in every theme
caption: airpods, airpods-case, airpod-left and airpod-right, generated against each theme's references (Classic, BeBox, Soft Be, Toybox, Papercraft, Enamel, Halftone), beside bluetooth and sound.

title: Preferences on a short screen
caption: A panel taller than the screen (AirPods, 752 points, on a 700-point display) opens as tall as fits, laid out at its own size and scrolled, with a scroll bar the window is widened for. Panels that fit are unchanged.

title: Tracker: Go to File or Folder
caption: Go ▸ Go to File or Folder… (⇧⌘G): a path copied is in the field already, selected, so Return goes; the names in its folder that what's typed could be are listed as it's typed, Tab completes, ↑↓ choose. A folder opens; a file shows selected in its folder's window.

title: Deskbar: the speaker's menu
caption: Right-click the speaker: every output and input, mute, and while AirPods play, their levels, noise control, Conversation Awareness, Personalized Volume, music or call quality, and both settings panels.

title: Command palette: every setting in Preferences
caption: Each control in every Preferences panel is a palette result, named with its panel, tab and box, and found by the words people use for it elsewhere ('night shift' finds Night Mode). The index is made from the panels as they're drawn, so a new setting is found without listing it.

title: A setting found is shown, lit
caption: Chosen in the palette, Preferences opens the setting's panel (on its tab, clicked if need be) with the control ringed in the keyboard-navigation colour for a moment: olo_ui::spotlight, which any app or agent can use to say 'here'. Two lines wide on device pixels; frames only while it comes and goes.

title: Command palette: Go to the path in the clipboard
caption: With a path copied (absolute, ~/…, a file:// URI), the palette offers to go there before anything is typed, and a path typed whole is offered too: Tracker shows it, a folder in its window, a file selected in its folder's. Read off the UI thread once the palette has the keyboard, which app_server now gives an exclusive layer as it shows.

title: Text cut short shows whole in a tip
caption: Resting the pointer on text the kit cut with … (here a name in Tracker's column) shows all of it in the kit's tip; with ⌘ held, at once. Every kit window does it for every label it cuts or that runs past its clip.

title: A window tab's cut title shows whole
caption: app_server shows the whole title of a window whose tab cuts it short on a tooltip's plate under the tab, once the pointer rests on the title (at once with ⌘), as Olo's apps do for their cut text.

title: Terminal: text kept legible on any background
caption: Before (top) and after: colours a program picked for a dark terminal (pale greys and blues, bright white) or bands it drew (diff lines, a composer's grey) left text nearly invisible in light mode. Now text keeps WCAG's 4.5:1 against its cell, moved toward black or white just as far as it takes, its hue kept; box drawing and blocks as drawn; faint text still faint.

title: Tracker: Open With and Always Open With
caption: A file's menu offers a few apps that suit its kind (its default marked, Olo's own, then those that say they open it), and Always Open With makes one the kind's default for Olo and for other programs.

title: Preferences: Default Apps
caption: A new panel: each kind of file and link with the app it opens in, changeable from the apps that suit it; a choice is the kind's for Olo and for other programs (Tracker's Always Open With chooses too). Its icon, a document with Olo's application cube, from the reference set.

title: Tracker: Open With ▸ Other…
caption: Any app can open a file: Other… lists every app that opens files, found by typing part of its name, with 'Always open files like … with it'.

title: Default Apps: your own kinds
caption: Preferences ▸ Default Apps ▸ Your Own Kinds: a kind named by its extensions (Game saves: .sav .sv2) opens in the app chosen; Olo knows files by it everywhere (olo_xdg::mime::own_kinds).

title: Default Apps: what Open With offers
caption: The Open With tab: a kind's apps in Open With ▸, in order, moved, removed and added; Olo's Choice lets Olo choose again.

title: File panels: Open With
caption: An item's menu in the Open and Save panels: Quick Look, Open With ▸ (the kit's olo_ui::open_with, as Tracker's) and Show in Tracker.

title: Sound: Voice Processing
caption: Every microphone through Olo's voice processing (echo cancellation, DeepFilterNet noise suppression, level), and what it is doing now, in a line. Here against a sandboxed sound server's made-up devices.

title: Deskbar: voice processing in the speaker's menu
caption: Right-click the speaker: Clean Up Microphone Sound, and in a submenu what it's tuned for, how much background noise to take out, echo and level (through olo-voice --set, as an agent would).

title: Focus: an alert from a covered app shows
caption: In Focus mode an alert that names no window (here StyledEdit's 'Save changes?' while Tracker is in front; Passwords' passkey question over Chrome) shows over the window in front, with the keyboard, instead of staying hidden with its app.

title: File panel: the look floats
caption: Space in a file panel (here the portal's, as Slack asks) looks at the file in a floating window over the panel, never a tile.

title: Telegram: Unknown Senders
caption: People who aren't contacts and were never written to get a list of their own under the archive: no notification, no unread count, until written back to. Avatars are 40 pt, from 46.

title: Telegram: chats chosen together
caption: ⌘-click, ⇧-click or Edit ▸ Select All Chats chooses several; their menu archives, unarchives, marks read, mutes or deletes them all (asking first).

title: Olo Suggestions
caption: A new app: what Olo suggests, none of it needed, each applied with a button or all with Apply All. The first: brush, the bash-compatible shell in Rust, as the login shell.

title: Olo Suggestions: applied, and undone
caption: What's applied is listed with a button that undoes it (here: Use bash Again).

title: Menus taller than the screen scroll
caption: A kit menu longer than its display stops short of its edges and scrolls: an arrow at each end there's more past scrolls it while the pointer rests there; the wheel and the keys too. Here Default Apps' every app, at the top and scrolled to the end.

title: Banners over Deskbar's menu (before)
caption: Before: a notification banner, a Top layer surface that came after Deskbar, drew over Deskbar's menus and took their clicks.

title: Deskbar's menus over banners
caption: Layer surfaces' menus are drawn and hit-tested over the whole Top layer, so Deskbar's menus are over any banner (shell::layer_menus).

title: Quick Look from a file panel (before)
caption: Before: the look, a process of its own with no parent, opened in a cascade slot at the asking app's corner, half over the panel.

title: Quick Look centred over the file panel
caption: The panel exports its window (xdg-foreign, Window::export_handle) and the Viewer opens the look over it (--over=); app_server keeps a dialog that sizes itself after opening centred over its parent until it's moved.

title: Agent Screens: a screen renamed
caption: Screen ▸ Rename… or a click on its title: the name the person gives shows in the list and the header, kept with its history (olo-screen rename NAME TITLE; list says it).

title: Agent Screens: several chosen, archived, deleted
caption: ⌘- and ⇧-clicks or ⌘A choose screens together; their menu archives, unarchives, stops or deletes them all (asked once); View ▸ Show Archived lists the archived in their own section; Delete moves histories to the Trash.

title: Emoji picker: five from AI for a description
caption: ⌃⌘Space opens the emoji picker over everything: search as you type, a tab a group, skin tones kept; ⌘↩ asks the model chosen in Preferences ▸ AI for five emoji for what was typed, each with its reason. Return puts the selected one into the field that had the keyboard, in any app (app_server's InsertText). (A fake model answered here; tests never call a real one.)

title: Preferences ▸ AI: Emoji
caption: The emoji picker's AI suggestions get their own switch, model and effort (low by default: they're asked while you wait), as Smart Tiling has; the panel grows to fit them.

title: Telegram: changes kept until Telegram has them
caption: Archiving, reading, muting and pinning go into an outbox on disk and leave it only once Telegram has them, sent again on the next start if need be. A line under the chat list shows them going; quitting waits up to 30 s for them (Quit Now quits at once; what's left is kept). The demo account, its changes slowed down to show it.

title: Agent Screens: Live at the screen's own frame rate
caption: Live now shows the agent screen's own frames, shared with the person's compositor as dmabufs (a subsurface of the window), at up to 120 frames a second; before, it took up to eight pictures a second and resampled each on the CPU (30% of a core while the screen moved, 0.6% now). The frame line round the picture stays flush at every scale.

title: Preferences ▸ Terminal: tell coding agents to use Agent Screens
caption: A third Coding Agents setting: Claude Code and Codex are told as they start to test and use desktop apps and web pages on Agent Screens of their own, and how, Olo's Chrome included, so they never start a Chrome on the person's screen. The panel is taller to fit it.

title: Text fields scroll to the caret, and show cut text in a tip
caption: A one-line field used to always show its start: typing past its end hid the caret and what was typed (top, before). Now it scrolls sideways while edited, keeping the caret in view (middle). Unfocused, it shows its start again, and the whole text is in a tip on hover (bottom). Never a password's.

title: Preferences ▸ Touchpad ▸ Touch: Train for Your Palm
caption: A guided run through five exercises on the touchpad, each shown as an Olo-style animation of hands on a pad (left) and mirrored live by what the pad sees (right: a palm in orange, a finger in blue), with a word on how it's going and how many more touches it needs. Then Olo's hand-written palm model is refined to the person's hands off the UI thread, kept in the settings, and tried live.

title: Train for Your Palm, in a dialog of its own
caption: The palm trainer moved out of the Touch tab (where it ran off the panel) into a 560×440 dialog opened from a button. The film is a laptop's deck, keys and the pad between the palm rests, with the hands resting and lifting; beside it the pad live, its own shape, each touch drawn as the model calls it: here one hand's palm half over the left edge, which the size rule misses (the red ring) and the model catches. A sixth exercise gathers exactly that case.

title: StyledEdit's tool bars
caption: The kit's new ToolBar: StyledEdit's file, editing and format tools along the top (wrapping to two rows in a narrow window, a » menu for what still doesn't fit), insert and view tools down the side. Every tool is a menu command and shows its state (Bold and Center pushed for the selected title); the pickers show the font, size and colour where the selection starts. 25 new icons, in every theme.

title: Backup takes passwords to another computer
caption: Preferences ▸ Backup seals passwords and sign-ins into the backup with a password, and moves it in on another computer: paths under the new home, the Token Pool paused, Telegram signed in again; what an import left behind is listed.

title: Train for Your Palm: one thing a step, and a banner when it's done
caption: Each of the twelve exercises asks one thing, with a line under the title saying what to do now (rest, hold, point, lift) from the hands on the pad; a finished step gets a green banner in the place of the status line (the kit's new Banner), and the key caps sit level with their labels at every scale.

title: Sound ▸ Voice Processing ▸ Try It
caption: A few seconds of your voice, recorded and put through each setting worth comparing: what each adds (delay, its time a 10 ms frame, what noise suppression and levelling did) and what ran it; played as the original or the chosen setting's sound, switching at the same place, with a live spectrum of both (the kit's new Spectrum).

title: Terminal: tile mode's group headers selected while their groups show
caption: With every group tiled (the default), each group's header is drawn selected; a click takes that group out of the tiles and another brings it back.

title: Terminal: Hide When Tiled
caption: A tab's menu hides it from Tile All Tabs: it stays in the strip with its icon and title faded, and the tiles share the window without it.

title: Terminal: the side strip lined up
caption: Down the side, the tabs' icons, the groups' names and New Tab's + sit under the menu bar's first title, the first chip clears the menu bar as it does along the top, and the pane heads beside it are as tall as the top strip.

title: Command palette: every text key, and Ctrl for files
caption: Text editing's keys are commands of their own (Move to the end of the line, ⌘→), done in the window the palette opened over; files and folders come with a tap of Ctrl, as the key hint at the field's right says.

title: Terminal: a slim scroll bar, there when wanted
caption: The kit's SlimScrollBar over the scrollback's right edge: shown when the pointer comes near or the view scrolls, wider under the pointer, fading a moment after; its thumb drags and its track pages.

title: Terminal ▸ Command Suggestions: brush's hints from a model of your own
caption: Preferences ▸ Terminal turns on olo-complete, a tiny model of your own commands (the line, the folder, the commands before in that shell, the hour and the day) that gives brush its grey hint. Turning it on starts it and runs its first fine-tune from the history, then says how it did on your newest commands; it learns again a minute after you type. Unavailable while brush isn't the login shell, and a brush from before the model is told apart by a mark in its binary, each with a button to Olo Suggestions. The pane is 520×692 for its tallest state.

title: Activity Monitor ▸ AI: how the command model does
caption: A new section, asked of olo-complete once a second only while it shows: suggestions offered and taken (whole or a word at a time), what it knows, latency from the question to the answer sent (typically, 95th percentile, slowest) with a graph, and its learning: fine-tunes, the last one's examples, steps and time, how often its first suggestion is right on the newest commands against the hand-written weights, and whether it was kept. Off, it says so, with Terminal Preferences… to turn it on.
